history.citation: 몰몬교 종교 광신교 - 교회와 당사국아침 택배 및 뉴욕 이루이 르 (뉴욕시, 뉴욕) 7, 아니오. 1333 (8월 31일).
history.teaser:
An 1831 newspaper article expressing skepticism and criticism towards Mormonism, depicting it as a product of religious excitement and ignorance.

Key Points:

  • Mormonism viewed as a mix of roguery, ingenuity, and ignorance
  • Originated in Western New York
  • Founders were simple, unknown individuals before Mormonism
  • Joseph Smith described as indolent and aimless
  • Money-digging activities linked to early Mormon leaders
  • Mormonism’s early practices related to seeking hidden treasures
  • Introduction of a money dreamer from Ohio to the group
  • Skeptical view of Mormonism’s religious and moral claims

history.citation: 몰몬 망상. 침례교 기록과 문학 등록기 (조지 타운, 켄터키) 2, 아니오. 9 (1831년 9월):135-36쪽. 햄프셔 가제트 (1831년 5월) 및 버몬트 크로니클에서 재 인쇄했다.
history.teaser:
A critical account from a Presbyterian in Ohio detailing the early activities and beliefs of the Mormon community, drawing comparisons to an earlier religious movement.

Key Points:

  • Public interest in Mormonism is high in Ohio
  • Mormon community practices communal living, the “bag family”
  • Joseph Smith, Jr. claims direct revelation from God
  • Smith purportedly performs miracles and reads people’s hearts
  • Attendee observes unusual spiritual manifestations at a meeting
  • Methodists, Baptists, and Presbyterians have joined the Mormons
  • Comparisons made to the “Pilgrims” religious movement and its downfall
  • Editor suggests Mormonism may end similarly to the “Pilgrims”

history.citation: 몰몬 종교 - 직업적 야망 - 웨스턴 뉴욕 - 몰몬성은 Uhio를 갔다. 아침 택배와 뉴욕 핵심 (뉴욕시, 뉴욕) 7, 아니오. 1331 (1831년 9월 1일).
history.teaser:
An article from the Morning Courier and New-York Enquirer discussing the origins and criticisms of the Mormon religion, and its migration to Ohio.

Key Points:

  • Religious excitement and revival in New York
  • Efforts to blend religious and worldly concerns
  • Western New York as the headquarters of religious zealots
  • Religious fanaticism led to the infatuation of Mormonism
  • Joseph Smith claimed to find golden plates
  • Book of Mormon believed to be authored by an ex-preacher from Ohio
  • Martin Harris played a significant role in financing the Book of Mormon
  • Mormonites established a community system in Ohio

history.author: O., W. [오웬, 윌리엄]
history.citation: O., W. [Owen, William]. "몰몬경 성경" 무료 Enquirer (뉴욕) (뉴욕) (1831년 9월 3일):364쪽.
history.teaser:
An early skeptical critique of the Book of Mormon, highlighting its parallels with the Bible and questioning its authenticity.

Key Points:

  • Encountered the Book of Mormon on a canal boat
  • Book aims to corroborate Old and New Testament doctrines
  • Describes Lehi’s journey to avoid Jerusalem’s destruction
  • Smith claimed to translate the book from brass plates
  • Ten witnesses hefted the plates, three saw them with an angel
  • Story includes Nephites and Lamanites, wars, and Christ’s appearance
  • Perceived as a parody of the Bible by the critic
  • Described as well-composed but ridiculed for its claims

history.author: 오웬, 윌리엄
history.citation: 오웬, 윌리엄. "몰몬경의 비교와 이론과 새로운 증언의 성경, 또는 황금 성경 vs. 성경책." 무료 Enquirer (NewYork) (1831년 9월 10일):367-68쪽.
history.teaser:
An article comparing the Book of Mormon with the Old and New Testaments, suggesting similarities and considering the Book of Mormon’s impact on Christian belief.

Key Points:

  • Article discusses similarities between the Book of Mormon and the Bible
  • Suggests Book of Mormon corroborates the Bible
  • Notes both books’ historical and miraculous narratives
  • Compares figures and events in both books
  • Mentions the peaceful and moral nature of Mormons
  • Considers the Book of Mormon’s authenticity evidence for the Bible’s divinity
  • Describes the historical narrative of the Nephites and Lamanites
  • Notes the Book of Mormon’s growing followers and their migration plans

history.citation: 몰몬교 데이튼 저널 및 광고주 (Dayton, Ohio) 5, 아니오. 45 (10월 4일 1831년 10월):1쪽. 신시내티 가제 (1831년 9월 26일)에서 재판었다.
history.teaser:
An early critical newspaper article discussing the origins and expansion of Mormonism, focusing on Joseph Smith and the publication of the Book of Mormon.

Key Points:

  • Mormonites extended in Western New York and Eastern Ohio
  • Joseph Smith described as ignorant and indolent
  • Smiths engaged in digging for buried money
  • Joseph Smith claimed to find golden plates
  • Book of Mormon published with finances from Harris
  • Smith exhibited as a divinely inspired prophet
  • Mormons emigrated to Missouri seeking a promised land
  • Book of Mormon criticized as a gross imposition

history.author: 기멜
history.citation: 돼지. "몰몬경" 기독교계 워치 만 (보스톤) 12, 아니오. 40 (10월 7일 1831년 10월).
history.teaser:
A critical review of the Book of Mormon published in a Boston newspaper, questioning its divine origin and historical accuracy.

Key Points:

  • Book of Mormon claimed as divine revelation, substituting the Bible
  • Joseph Smith claimed translation from metallic plates
  • Plates’ inscriptions allegedly by prophets, starting with Nephi
  • Account includes improbable journey from Jerusalem to the Red Sea
  • Description of Arabian journey and settlement in promised land (America)
  • No external evidence for the book’s history, reliant on Smith’s translation
  • Book’s doctrine similar to Free-Will Baptists, contains “important truths”
  • Critical of the book’s claim to prophecy and divine inspiration

history.citation: 몰몬성. 트럼펫과 유니버얼리스트 잡지 보스턴, 매사추세츠) N.S. 2, 아니오. 17 (22월 22일 1831년 10월 181일):68쪽. 햄프셔 구조, 10월 1831년 경에서 재 인쇄했다.
history.teaser:
An article from the Trumpet and Universalist Magazine reporting on the migration and beliefs of early Mormons.

Key Points:

  • Mormonites migrating from Ohio to Missouri, their “promised land”
  • Some migrants included two merchants and respectable farmers
  • One convert’s property was estimated at $7,000
  • A Boston woman investigates Mormonism, becomes a convert
  • Convert believes the Book of Mormon to be a revelation from God
  • Converts believe leaders are true prophets and can perform miracles
  • Report of a sick person miraculously restored to health
  • Woman was a Methodist before converting to Mormonism

history.author: 부스, 에스라
history.citation: 몰몬교 - 아니. III. Ezra Booth to Rev. I. Eddy, 10 월 1831년 10월 24일. 오하이오 스타 (Ravenna, Ohio) (Ravenna, Ohio) (1831년 10월 27일).
history.teaser:
A letter from Ezra Booth to Rev. I. Eddy, published in the Ohio Star, offering a critical view of early Mormon practices and beliefs.

Key Points:

  • Mormonism’s character has changed from its early days.
  • Booth criticizes the “wonders” that early Mormons wished to forget.
  • Describes the practice of speaking in tongues as delirium.
  • Claims of receiving divine commission for preaching were discredited.
  • Visions of the New Jerusalem and the ten tribes were popular.
  • Angelic visitations were frequently claimed but seldom detailed.
  • Smith claimed to converse with celestial beings with “spiritual eyes.”
  • Booth skeptical of the three witnesses’ testimony of the golden plates.

history.author: 부스, 에스라
history.citation: 몰몬교 - 아니. vi. Ezra Booth to Rev. I. Eddy, 1831년 11월 14일. 오하이오 스타 (Ravenna, Ohio) (1831년 11월 17일).
history.teaser:
A letter by Ezra Booth expressing skepticism and criticism towards Mormonism, particularly focusing on the attempts to convert Native Americans and the establishment of Zion in Missouri.

Key Points:

  • Mormonites aim to convert Indians, similar to Jesuits in South America
  • Independence, Missouri, is the headquarters of the Mormonites
  • No Indians had embraced Mormonism at the time of writing
  • Mormonite teachings might inflame the Indians against whites
  • Foundation of Zion marked by a ceremony and laying of a symbolic cornerstone
  • Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon had high hopes but faced disappointments in Missouri
  • Smith and Rigdon planned to return to Ohio for a “great work”
  • Smith commanded not to labor and expected the Church to support him

history.citation: 몰몬성 물질. Christian Intelligencer And Eastern Chronicle (Gardiner, Maine) (1831년 11월 18일):184쪽. 일리노이스 애국자 (Jacksonville, 일리노이)에서 재판 (16 1831년 9월).
history.teaser:
An early account of a Mormon preacher’s visit and lecture, detailing the origins of the Book of Mormon and the beliefs of its followers.

Key Points:

  • Mormon preacher visited and lectured for over two hours
  • Origin story involves an angel visiting a young man
  • Young man found gold plates with Arabic characters
  • Plates described as being connected with rings
  • Preacher claimed to decipher hieroglyphics using stones
  • Mormon Bible described as indispensable
  • Mention of Laman, Nephi, and Lehigh as progenitors of Mormon
  • Preacher joined the sect due to discrepancies in other religions

history.citation: 몰몬교 오하이오 스타 (Ravenna, Ohio) (1831년 11월 24일).
history.teaser:
An article in the Ohio Star discussing the impact of Mr. Booth’s letters on exposing Mormonism to the public.

Key Points:

  • Mr. Booth’s letter is considered very interesting
  • Belief that the letters are influencing many deluded by Mormonism
  • Exposure of Mormonism seen as an important duty
  • Announcement that the letters will soon conclude

history.author: 부스, 에스라
history.citation: 부스, Ezra. "몰몬교 - 아니. Vii. " 오하이오 스타. (Portage County, Ohio) 2, 아니오. 47 (1831년 11월 24일). [읽을 수없는 텍스트]
history.teaser:
An account by Ezra Booth, a former Mormon, detailing his disillusionment with the Church and its leaders, particularly focusing on Joseph Smith’s actions and prophecies.

Key Points:

  • Ezra Booth writes to the Bishop of the Mormon Church in Missouri.
  • Discusses the secular business of the Church and land ownership.
  • Mentions contradictions and failures in prophecies and visions.
  • Describes internal conflicts within the Church leadership.
  • Expresses his decision to leave the Mormon Church.
  • Criticizes the commandments as being manipulative and inconsistent.
  • Highlights issues with the mission to the Indians and Sidney Rigdon’s exaggerations.
  • Booth calls for honesty and criticizes the Church’s false prophecies.

history.citation: 몰몬성 물질. 침례교 기록과 문학 등록기 (조지 타운, 켄터키) 2, 아니오. 12 (12 월 1831):272쪽.
history.teaser:
An early account of the origin of the Book of Mormon as presented by a follower, highlighting the supernatural aspects of its discovery.

Key Points:

  • A young man in Ontario county, N.Y., visited by an angel
  • Angel appeared three times in one night
  • Young man found gold plates with Arabic characters
  • Plates described as connected by rings, resembling the letter D
  • Also found two stones for translating the hieroglyphics
  • Translation performed with the stones placed over eyes
  • Resulted in the Book of Mormon, considered second to none
  • Claimed that the Holy Bible would be of little use without it

history.citation: 몰몬교 진리의 전당 (필라델피아) (12 월 1831):406-7쪽. Broome County Courier (Binghamton, New York)에서 재 인쇄 (빙하튼) (1831년 12월 22일).
history.teaser:
An early critique of Mormonism and its founders, portraying them as cunning and delusional.

Key Points:

  • Mormonism described as a result of religious excitement and ingenuity
  • Founders characterized as simple, cunning, and hypocritical
  • Joe Smith and others aimed to get rich through treasure digging
  • Religious plot conceived to give credibility to their treasure digs
  • Joe Smith declared the chosen one to reveal the Book of Mormon
  • Book of Mormon suggested to be authored by an ex-preacher
  • Financial support for printing Book of Mormon raised through mortgaging a farm
  • Mormon followers described as infatuated and abandoning families for promised land

history.citation: 몰몬교 - 노스. Viii-ix. 편지 VIII, 11월 29일, Ezra Booth to Rev. I. Eddy. 오하이오 스타 (Ravenna, Ohio) 2, 아니오. 49 (1831년 12월 8일):1쪽.
history.teaser:
A critical letter by Ezra Booth published in the Ohio Star newspaper discussing Mormonism, its claims about Native Americans, and its leadership under Joseph Smith.

Key Points:

  • Ezra Booth expresses skepticism about the origin of Native Americans.
  • Claims the Book of Mormon reveals Native Americans as a branch of Israel.
  • Describes a mission to the Indians led by Oliver Cowdery.
  • Revelation claims only Joseph Smith can receive commandments for the Church.
  • Cowdery allowed to speak but not write commandments.
  • Booth criticizes the credibility and authority of Joseph Smith.
  • Mentions suppression of other sources of revelation within the Church.
  • Describes challenges to Smith’s authority from within the Church.

history.author: 시드니 릭던, 1793-1876
history.citation: 리거, 시드니. "대중에게." 오하이오 스타 (Ravenna, Ohio) (12월 15일).
history.teaser:
Sidney Rigdon’s public challenge to detractors of the Book of Mormon, including a planned lecture on the Christian Religion and a direct invitation for a public debate.

Key Points:

  • Rigdon to deliver a lecture on the Christian Religion
  • Lecture scheduled for the village of Ravenna
  • Rigdon challenges Ezra Booth over his critical letters
  • Offers to review Booth’s letters publicly
  • Rigdon invites Simons Rider for a public investigation
  • Seeks to correct any delusions about the Book of Mormon
  • Wants to relieve public anxiety about the book
  • Seeks acceptance or rejection through Ohio Star

history.author: 부스, 에스라
history.citation: 몰몬교 - 노스. XIII-IX. 편지 IX, 1831년 12월 6일, Ezra Booth to Rev. I. Eddy. 오하이오 스타 (Ravenna, Ohio) 2, 아니오. 49 (1831년 12월 8일):1쪽.
history.teaser:
A letter by Ezra Booth to Rev. I. Eddy, criticizing Mormonism and detailing failed missionary efforts to Native Americans.

Key Points:

  • Ezra Booth critiques the credibility of Mormonism.
  • Describes Sidney Rigdon’s vision confirming the Book of Mormon.
  • Discusses failed missionary efforts to Native Americans.
  • Oliver Cowdery’s mission to the Indians ended by U.S. agent.
  • Plans for a City and Temple among the Gentiles, not Indians.
  • Attempts to gain access to Indian territories through trade.
  • Revelation encourages marrying Native Americans to spread Mormonism.
  • Booth’s intention to warn others about Mormonism.

history.citation: Sidney Rigdon. ...에 . Painesville Telegraph (오하이오주 페인즈빌) (1831년 12월 20일).
history.teaser:
An article from the Painesville Telegraph discussing Sidney Rigdon’s challenge to debate the authenticity of the Book of Mormon.

Key Points:

  • Sidney Rigdon, associated closely with Joseph Smith, issued a challenge
  • Challenge for a verbal debate on the Book of Mormon’s truth
  • Challenge directed at Mr. Booth and Deacon Rider, ex-Mormons
  • Rigdon previously challenged the world to disprove the Book of Mormon
  • Refused to meet Elder Campbell for a debate

history.author: 라이더, 사이먼즈
history.citation: 라이더, Symonds. "씨. 편집자." 오하이오 스타 (Ravenna, Ohio) (1831년 12월 29일).
history.teaser:
A letter to the editor by Symonds Ryder criticizing Mormonism and Sidney Rigdon’s challenge for a public debate on its validity.

Key Points:

  • Ryder considers Mormonism a base imposition
  • Rigdon challenged Ryder to a public debate on Mormonism
  • Ryder suggests a private meeting would be more productive
  • Ryder criticizes Rigdon’s temperament and mental state
  • Public interest in Mormonism in Hiram has waned
  • Rigdon’s challenge seen as a desperate act for attention
  • Rigdon previously rejected a polite challenge from Elder Thomas Campbell
  • Ryder discusses the implications of accepting Mormon commandments

history.author: 토울, 낸시
history.citation: 워싱트, 낸시. 유럽 및 아메리카, 137-47의 Nancy Towle의 경험에 삽화를 보여줍니다. 찰스턴 : 제안, 1832.
history.teaser:
Nancy Towle’s account of her encounter with early Mormons in Ohio, expressing skepticism and disapproval.

Key Points:

  • Nancy Towle traveled to Ohio to investigate Mormons.
  • She initially viewed them as a deluded people.
  • Joseph Smith claimed to have received golden plates from an angel.
  • The Book of Mormon is considered an inspired word by followers.
  • Mormon teachings include baptism, communal living, and miracles.
  • Towle found many leaving families to join Mormons in Missouri.
  • She personally rejects Mormon beliefs and criticizes their practices.
  • Towle vows to speak and write against Mormonism.

history.author: 시드니 릭던, 1793-1876
history.citation: 리거, 시드니. "대중에게." 오하이오 스타 (Ravenna, Ohio) (1월 12일).
history.teaser:
Sidney Rigdon’s public challenge to Simons Rider to defend his accusations against the Book of Mormon in the Ohio Star.

Key Points:

  • Rigdon invited Simons Rider to discuss the Book of Mormon’s authenticity
  • Rigdon accuses Rider of avoiding the challenge
  • Claims Rider hides behind reproach and abuse instead of evidence
  • Rigdon uses biblical reference to highlight Rider’s evasion
  • Suggests Rider’s accusations are unfounded and cowardly
  • Emphasizes the importance of openly defending one’s accusations
  • Rigdon offers a standing challenge to investigate the Book of Mormon’s claims
  • Leaves the matter publicly, suggesting Rider reconsider his approach

history.citation: 몰몬교 Cherokee Phoenix (뉴 이코타, 조지아) 4 (1832년 1월 21일). 보스턴 택배 (보스톤, 매사추세츠)에서 1831년 10월에서 재판. [불법적 인 텍스트]
history.teaser:
An article from the Cherokee Phoenix discussing the spread and impact of Mormonism, including missionary efforts and communal living principles.

Key Points:

  • Writer formerly a respectable citizen of Boston
  • Mormonism causes great excitement
  • About 100 souls humbled themselves for baptism
  • Church structure includes elders, priests, teachers, and deacons
  • Missionaries preaching to Native Americans
  • Three hundred converts in Ohio, communal property contributions
  • Communal living as natural consequence of Apostolic doctrine
  • Visitation by angels and revelation through a seer

history.citation: 씨. 부스. ...에 . 오하이오 스타 (Ravenna, Ohio) (183년 1월 26일).
history.teaser:
A newspaper editorial discussing a dispute between Mr. Booth and Mr. Rigdon regarding the Book of Mormon and its authenticity.

Key Points:

  • Mr. Booth defends his character against attacks by Mr. Rigdon
  • Booth questions the wisdom of trusting those who assert the Book of Mormon’s authenticity
  • Implies those asserting authenticity could be capable of dishonesty
  • Newspaper declines to publish Booth’s vindication to avoid obligation for a reply

history.citation: 몰몬교 Fredonia Censor (뉴욕) (뉴욕) (3월 7일). 프랭클린 민주당 (펜실베니아)에서 인쇄 된 프랭클린 (펜실베이니아)에서 인쇄했습니다.
history.teaser:
An early 1832 newspaper article detailing the beliefs and teachings of the Mormonites as they began to spread their religion in Pennsylvania.

Key Points:

  • Mormon missionaries visited Venango county, Pennsylvania
  • Joseph Smith received divine guidance to find gold plates
  • Gold plates contained an unknown language, translated by Smith
  • The Book of Mormon is another revelation to the house of Joseph
  • Lehi left Jerusalem, landing in South America, according to the Book of Mormon
  • Christianity flourished in the Americas for generations, then faded
  • Last prophet, Mormon, hid the plates to be found by a “gentile people”
  • Mormon missionaries predicted the imminent return of Jesus Christ

history.author: 스키너, 돌푸스
history.citation: 스키너, 돌마. "몰몬경의 변화" 복음의 잡지와 복음 옹호 (Utica, New York) 3, 아니오. 11 (1832년 3월 17일):67쪽.
history.teaser:
An article discussing a reported shift in Mormon theology towards universal salvation, prompting skepticism from the author.

Key Points:

  • New revelation reported among Mormonites about universal salvation
  • Revelation proclaimed by their seer, Jo Smith
  • Mormonites seeking forgiveness from those they previously cursed
  • Comparison made with Jews’ misunderstanding in the days of Jesus
  • Concern expressed about Mormonites aligning with Universalism
  • Previous Mormon teachings emphasized the doctrine of endless misery
  • Mormon Bible’s teachings on endless damnation highlighted
  • Assertion that embracing Universalism would require renouncing Mormonism

history.citation: 몰몬의 해나. 카톨릭 전신 (신시내티, 오하이오) 1 (4월 1832일):204-5쪽. 4월 183243년 경 Mercer Press (펜실베니아)에서 재 인쇄했다.
history.teaser:
A detailed account of early Mormon missionaries’ visit and teachings, as recounted in a secular newspaper.

Key Points:

  • Missionaries claimed to be sent by God to preach the gospel
  • Joseph Smith found plates after an angel’s visitation
  • Smith translated the plates with divine inspiration
  • Lehi’s journey to South America and division of his people
  • Final battle among these groups happened where the plates were found
  • Mormonite Bible connects and fulfills prophecies of Isaiah
  • Missionaries work without compensation, relying on faith
  • Joseph Smith, Cowdery, Whitmer, and Harris testify to seeing the plates

history.citation: 선택된. 저녁과 아침 별 (독립, 미주리) 1, 아니오. 1 (6 월 1832) : [3].
history.teaser:
An editorial in the first issue of The Evening and the Morning Star discussing the authenticity and origin of the New Testament in relation to the Book of Mormon.

Key Points:

  • Prophecy extract from the Book of Mormon shared
  • New Testament parts believed taken from Book of Mormon
  • Alleged tampering by the “Mother of Harlots”
  • Period of tampering estimated between A.D. 460 to 1400
  • Command given for a new translation of the Bible
  • King James’ translators did well but lacked revelation

history.citation: [몰몬경에서]. 저녁과 아침 별 (독립, 미주리) 1, 아니오. 1 (6 월 1832):8쪽.
history.teaser:
An early publication in the LDS church’s newspaper featuring a message from the Book of Mormon aimed at Gentiles to repent and be baptized.

Key Points:

  • Message directed to the Gentiles
  • Words commanded by Jesus Christ
  • Call to turn from wicked ways and repent
  • Mentions specific sins to repent from
  • Invitation to be baptized in Christ’s name
  • Promises remission of sins and the Holy Ghost
  • Opportunity to be numbered with the house of Israel

history.citation: 몰몬경 저녁과 아침 별 (독립, 미주리) 1, 아니오. 1 (6 월 1832) : [6].
history.teaser:
An article from the first issue of The Evening and the Morning Star encouraging inquiry into the truth of the Book of Mormon through biblical prophecy and archaeological evidence.

Key Points:

  • Encourages honest inquiry into the truth of the Book of Mormon
  • Links the Book of Mormon to the tribe of Joseph from Genesis
  • References Ezekiel 37’s “Stick of Ephraim” as possible evidence
  • Mentions Isaiah’s prophecy of a “marvelous work” linking to the Book
  • Points to archaeological remains as silent evidence of a civilized people
  • Advises seeking divine confirmation for truth seekers

history.citation: 몰몬교 표준 (신시내티, 오하이오) (1832년 6월 1일):4쪽.
history.teaser:
An early critical view of Mormonism from a local Ohio newspaper, highlighting concerns about its rapid growth and practices.

Key Points:

  • Mormonism seen as an ominous sign of change
  • Boasts hundreds of converts, threatening thousands
  • Deemed a cunningly formed plot covered by sanctimonious appearances
  • Converts include members from almost all denominations, especially Free Baptists
  • Success of Mormonism difficult to calculate
  • Many converts hadn’t read the Book of Mormon before joining
  • Smith’s word is seen as the word of God by followers
  • Mormons preparing to move to a promised land in Missouri Territory

history.citation: 몰몬교,Painesville Telegraph (오하이오주 페인즈빌) 4, 아니오. 1 (1832년 6월 21일). 개척자 (록 스프링스, 일리노이 주)에서 복각했습니다.
history.teaser:
An article from the Painesville Telegraph discusses the impact of Mormon missionaries in Illinois, focusing on the conversion and subsequent mental breakdown of a local Methodist preacher and his wife.

Key Points:

  • Mormon preachers visited Illinois counties
  • Some families were ‘almost persuaded’ to convert
  • Mr. McMahan, a Methodist preacher, converted to Mormonism
  • McMahan attempted to work miracles and became deranged
  • McMahan and his wife attacked their house and furniture

history.teaser:
A critical account by E. D. Howe challenging the origins, content, and claims of the Book of Mormon.

Key Points:

  • E.D. Howe critiques the origin story of the American Indians as described in the Book of Mormon.
  • Questions the priesthood and sacrifices mentioned, comparing to biblical standards.
  • Highlights inconsistencies with biblical teachings and historical timelines.
  • Challenges the use of the Egyptian language by ancient Jews as described.
  • Examines prophecies and teachings in the Book of Mormon related to Christ.
  • Discusses the impossibility of certain events and teachings pre-Christ.
  • Questions the translation process of the Book of Mormon plates.
  • Critiques the overall credibility and authenticity of the Book of Mormon.

history.teaser:
E. D. Howe’s “Mormonism Unvailed” is an early critical examination of the origins and claims of the Latter Day Saint movement, particularly focusing on Joseph Smith and the Book of Mormon. It compiles affidavits and statements from residents of Palmyra, New York, and Harmony, Pennsylvania, to challenge the character of Smith and the divine origin of the Book of Mormon. The document suggests that Smith’s claims of finding golden plates and translating them into the Book of Mormon were part of a broader pattern of deceit and manipulation.

  • Howe questions the credibility of the Book of Mormon witnesses.
  • Claims Smith family known for digging for treasure and deceit.
  • Joseph Smith’s character repeatedly called into question.
  • Assertions of Smith’s treasure-seeking behavior linked to Book of Mormon.
  • Allegations of Smith using a seer stone for treasure hunting.
  • Critiques of Smith’s moral character and allegations of dishonesty.
  • Smith accused of changing his story about the golden plates.
  • Community members express skepticism about Smith’s claims.

  • Expresses the challenge of convincing those already captivated by Mormonism

history.author: 하우, 에버 D., 1798년
history.citation: Howe, E. D. D. 몰몬경은 현재의 시간에부터는 단수 부과와 망상에 대한 충실한 설명. 전파기의 캐릭터의 스케치와 유명한 황금 성경이 세계에서 유명한 방식의 세부 사항이 있습니다. 추가 된 것, 그 성경의 역사적인 부분이 20 년 전의 솔로몬 스파 딩 (Solomon Spalding)에 의해 작성된 확률에 대한 문의가 20 년 전이며, 그 사람이 로맨스로 출판 된 것으로 의도 된 것으로 의도했다. 오하이오주 페인즈빌 : e. D. Howe, 1834.
history.teaser:
An early critical account of the origins of Mormonism, focusing on the roles of Joseph Smith, Sidney Rigdon, and Parley P. Pratt.

Key Points:

  • Parley P. Pratt converted after encountering Joseph Smith in Palmyra.
  • Sidney Rigdon, a preacher from Ohio, became a key figure in early Mormonism.
  • Expedition to convert the “Lamanites” led by Oliver Cowdery.
  • Joseph Smith provided revelations to guide the missionary efforts.
  • Emma Smith was commanded to be Joseph’s scribe and select hymns.
  • Smith and Rigdon claimed miraculous powers and performed baptisms.
  • Rigdon’s conversion marked a significant point in spreading Mormonism.
  • Mormonism’s early practices included speaking in tongues and prophesying.

history.author: 하우, 에버 D., 1798년
history.citation: Howe, E. D. D. 몰몬경은 현재의 시간에부터는 단수 부과와 망상에 대한 충실한 설명. 전파기의 캐릭터의 스케치와 유명한 황금 성경이 세계에서 유명한 방식의 세부 사항이 있습니다. 추가 된 것, 그 성경의 역사적인 부분이 20 년 전의 솔로몬 스파 딩 (Solomon Spalding)에 의해 작성된 확률에 대한 문의가 20 년 전이며, 그 사람이 로맨스로 출판 된 것으로 의도 된 것으로 의도했다. 오하이오주 페인즈빌 : e. D. Howe, 1834.
history.teaser:
A critical account of the origins of Mormonism, focusing on Joseph Smith and his family, and the publication of the Book of Mormon.

Key Points:

  • Describes the Smith family as lazy, indolent, and superstitious
  • Joseph Smith Jr. skilled in necromancy and divination
  • Joseph’s followers saw his ignorance as proof of divine mission
  • Martin Harris, a key financier, believed in Smith’s visions
  • Harris’s prophecies include drastic religious and political changes
  • Oliver Cowdery, another key figure, became an editor for Mormon publications
  • David Whitmer, a witness to the golden plates, described them in detail
  • Book questions the authenticity of the Book of Mormon’s origins

history.author: 휘트먼, 제이슨
history.citation: 휘트먼, 제이슨. "몰몬경" 단위 아리아리아 (보스톤) 1 (1834년 1월):40-50쪽.
history.teaser:
An analytical review of the Book of Mormon by Jason Whitman, providing a critical perspective on its content, style, and the strategies used by Mormon missionaries to spread their faith.

Key Points:

  • Book of Mormon presented as a new sacred scripture by Joseph Smith
  • Historical account involves ancient peoples migrating to the Americas
  • Review critiques the book’s attempt to imitate biblical style
  • Mentions prophecies and visions about Christ
  • Observes lack of Jewish customs, reflecting modern Christian practices instead
  • Discusses the book’s appeal to prejudices against established religious and social structures
  • Notes the strategy of confirming the faith through claimed miracles and speaking in tongues
  • Whitman expresses concern over people’s susceptibility to the Mormon message due to lack of biblical and historical knowledge

history.citation: 모로나이의 애도. 저녁과 아침 별 (Kirtland, Ohio) 2, 아니오. 16 (1834년 1월):128쪽.
history.teaser:
A lamentation poem attributed to Moroni, expressing grief over the destruction of the Nephite people.

Key Points:

  • Moroni is left without a home and mourns
  • He is pained by the sight of his people’s corpses
  • Moroni reflects on his father’s writings about the Nephites’ fear
  • Nephites were mercilessly killed by their enemies
  • Ten thousand led by Moroni died at the hill Cumorah
  • Moroni’s father despaired over the fallen Nephites’ beauty
  • Moroni yearns for death to join God and find peace
  • Moroni sang this lamentation observing the slain Nephites

history.citation: 몰몬교 개신교 표현식 및 교회 등록 (필라델피아) 5, 아니오. 1 (1 월 1834년 1월):8쪽. 1834년 1월 Circa Circa에서 재 인쇄했다.
history.teaser:
An article from 1834 commenting on the rapid spread of Mormonism as surprising given its origins and the doctrines of the Book of Mormon.

Key Points:

  • Doctrine finding advocates despite being considered absurd
  • Surprise at the rapid spread of Mormonism
  • Mormon preacher from Ohio and New Hampshire making a stir
  • Whole of Freewill Baptist Church converted to Mormonism
  • Thirty persons and their pastor re-baptized
  • Troubles faced by preachers in Andover

history.citation: 대중에게. Painesville Telegraph (오하이오주 페인즈빌) (1834년 1월 31일).
history.teaser:
A public statement by a committee in Kirtland, Ohio, aimed at discrediting Joseph Smith and the Book of Mormon, asserting it to be a work of fiction.

Key Points:

  • Committee formed in Kirtland, Ohio to investigate the Book of Mormon
  • Concerned about the societal impact of Joseph Smith’s followers
  • Committee employed D. P. Hurlbut for investigation
  • Aim to prove the Book of Mormon as fiction
  • Claims Book of Mormon written by Solomon Spalding
  • Seeks to discredit Joseph Smith’s honesty and prophetic claims

history.author: 브릭스, J. A.
history.citation: Briggs, J. A. "몰몬교의 기원" Christian Watchman (보스턴) (1834년 1월 31일).
history.teaser:
An article criticizing the origins and followers of Mormonism, including the Spaulding theory for the Book of Mormon’s creation.

Key Points:

  • Mormonism’s origin detailed by a former Mormon
  • Solomon Spaulding theorized as the original author
  • Spaulding’s manuscript supposedly copied by Mormons in Pittsburgh
  • Claims of similarities between Spaulding’s writings and the Book of Mormon
  • Mormons described as ignorant and deluded
  • Some Mormons have renounced their faith and returned to truth
  • Mormonism predicted to fail and scatter
  • Mormons arming themselves for conflict

history.author: 캠벨, 알렉산더, 1788-1866
history.citation: 캠벨, 알렉산더. "시간의 징후." 밀레니그 기념일 하이너 5, 아니오. 4 (1834년 4월) : 148, 주.
history.teaser:
A critical review by Alexander Campbell, dismissing the Book of Mormon as absurd and a deception.

Key Points:

  • Describes the Book of Mormon as a disgrace to Christianity
  • Calls the book a “bundle of lies” written by an atheist
  • Claims it’s a trick to make money, with a poor style
  • Considers it carries its own condemnation in every page
  • God never demands faith without evidence
  • The book illegally anticipates Christian practices before Christ
  • Argues against two simultaneous systems of salvation
  • No one can practice the religion of a future dispensation beforehand

history.author: 에디터 오브 더 스타
history.citation: 상당한 흥분. 저녁과 아침 별 (Kirtland, Ohio) 2, 아니오. 19 (4 월 1834):150쪽.
history.teaser:
An article discussing public reaction and legal proceedings against Doctor P. Hurlbut for threatening Joseph Smith Jr., and addressing misconceptions about Hurlbut’s intentions and qualifications.

Key Points:

  • Excitement among citizens regarding Doctor P. Hurlbut’s threats against Joseph Smith Jr.
  • Hurlbut held to bail for threatening Smith’s life
  • Public speculation and rumors spread about the legal case
  • Misconceptions about Hurlbut’s professional title and intentions clarified
  • Hurlbut’s claims to expose “Mormonism” debunked
  • Article criticizes those who support Hurlbut’s actions
  • Encourages lawful conduct and proper treatment of fellow men
  • Editor expresses confidence that truth will prevail despite Hurlbut’s efforts

history.citation: 다음은에서 가져온 것입니다. ...에 . 저녁과 아침 별 (Kirtland, Ohio) 2, 아니오. 19 (1834년 4월):151쪽.
history.teaser:
An article from The Evening and the Morning Star refuting a sensational story about a Mormon preacher’s alleged drowning during a failed miraculous act.

Key Points:

  • Story originated from the “Saturday Courier” of Philadelphia.
  • Claims of a Mormon preacher attempting to walk on water.
  • Alleged sabotage by “wicked Lamanites” who sawed his plank bridge.
  • Preacher supposedly drowned during a public demonstration.
  • Article criticizes the circulation of falsehoods against Mormons.
  • Challenges the claim that Mormonism is a delusion.
  • Questions the journalistic integrity of publishing such tales.
  • Editor sarcastically suggests the storyteller should write “religious lies.”

history.author: F., L.M.
history.citation: F., L. M. "몰몬 선지자와의 인터뷰." 복음주의 잡지와 복음 옹호 (Utica, 뉴욕) N.., 5, NO. 14 (1834년 4월 5일):107쪽.
history.teaser:
An article detailing a skeptical and critical account of an encounter with Joseph Smith, the founder of the Latter Day Saint movement.

Key Points:

  • Joseph Smith made an ordinary appearance at a Mormon meeting
  • Smith acknowledged disbelief in his revelations
  • Described as having a physical appearance and manner that do not command attention
  • Smith’s approach to preaching and revelation is criticized
  • The interviewer attempted to question Smith directly about his mission
  • Smith avoided providing direct evidence of his divine mission
  • The conversation ended with Smith leaving abruptly
  • The writer remains skeptical of Smith’s claims

history.citation: 몰몬 재판 Chardon Spectator와 Geaga Gazette (1834년 4월 12일).
history.teaser:
A newspaper article detailing a court case involving Joseph Smith, the founder of Mormonism, and Doctor P. Hurlburt, an ex-Mormon and critic of the faith.

Key Points:

  • Joseph Smith filed a complaint against Doctor P. Hurlburt
  • Hurlburt accused of threatening Smith’s safety
  • Case attracted great public interest and a crowded courtroom
  • Hurlburt was a former Mormon elder excommunicated for misconduct
  • After excommunication, Hurlburt criticized Mormonism and Joseph Smith
  • Hurlburt researched claims the Book of Mormon was plagiarized
  • Witnesses testified to Hurlburt’s threats against Smith
  • Court ordered Hurlburt to post a $200 bond to keep the peace

history.citation: 몰몬교 Susquehanna Register (몬트 로즈, 펜실베니아) 9, 아니오. 21 (5월 1일 1834).
history.teaser:
An 1834 article from the Susquehanna Register featuring affidavits questioning the character and claims of Joseph Smith, the founder of Mormonism, and the authenticity of the Book of Mormon.

Key Points:

  • Article responds to claims of forgery regarding Isaac Hale’s letter.
  • Isaac Hale provides a detailed account of Joseph Smith’s early activities.
  • Hale describes Smith’s involvement in “money-digging” and use of a “seer stone.”
  • Hale recounts Smith’s marriage to his daughter, Emma, and their move.
  • Smith claimed to have quit “glass-looking” but then found the Book of Plates.
  • Martin Harris and Oliver Cowdery played roles in translating the Book of Mormon.
  • Several affidavits declare Smith and his associates to be impostors and liars.
  • Community members affirm the good character of affidavit providers.

history.citation: 몰몬경 책. 미시간 Sentinel (5 월 1834년 5월 3일).
history.teaser:
An article from the Michigan Sentinel discussing efforts to discredit the Book of Mormon and Joseph Smith’s prophetic claims.

Key Points:

  • Ohio paper reports a committee investigating the Book of Mormon’s origin
  • Committee aims to prove the Book of Mormon is fictional
  • Claims Solomon Spalding wrote the book over twenty years ago
  • Research seeks to undermine Joseph Smith’s claims to prophecy
  • Efforts to expose Joseph Smith’s “speculations” among Ohioans
  • Article suggests Ohioans are too knowledgeable to convert to Mormonism

history.author: 검시관, F.E.
history.citation: 몰몬교 개신교 센티넬 (Schenectady, New York) N.S. 5, 아니오. 1 (1834년 6월 4일):4-5쪽. 뉴 잉글랜드 검토, Circa, Mormonism에서 재 인쇄했습니다.
history.teaser:
An article from the Protestant Sentinel reprinted from the New England Review discussing the history, beliefs, and practices of early Mormonism.

Key Points:

  • Joseph Smith found golden plates and spectacles in 1828
  • Smith claimed exclusive ability to translate the plates
  • Martin Harris assisted Smith and funded the Book of Mormon’s publication
  • Smith and followers moved west seeking the “land of promise”
  • Claims of miracles and divine communications among followers
  • Mormonites eventually settled in Jackson County, Missouri
  • Mormon creed compared to Mahometanism with Smith as a prophet
  • Mormon influence spread beyond New York, reaching New England

history.author: 스미스, 조셉, 1805-1844
history.citation: 조셉 스미스는 올리버 카우드리입니다. 저녁과 아침 별 (Kirtland, Ohio) 2, 아니오. 24 (1834년 9월):192쪽.
history.teaser:
A letter from Joseph Smith to Oliver Cowdery responding to criticism from Alexander Campbell, an influential religious leader.

Key Points:

  • Smith critiques Alexander Campbell’s negative stance on the Book of Mormon.
  • Joseph Smith has not personally met Alexander Campbell.
  • Campbell has shifted from direct criticism to more indirect remarks.
  • Smith suggests Campbell’s criticisms actually encourage investigation into the Book of Mormon.
  • Joseph Smith expresses satisfaction that opposition helps the truth of the Book of Mormon to be investigated.
  • Smith adheres to Christ’s teaching of turning the other cheek in response to Campbell’s attacks.
  • Joseph Smith remains committed to the testimony of the Book of Mormon.

history.author: 카우더리, 올리버
history.citation: 올리버 카우드리와 W.W. 펠프스, 1834년 9월 7일 후기 성도들의 메신저와 옹호 (Kirtland, Ohio) 1, 아니오. 1 (10 월 1834):13-16쪽.
history.teaser:
Oliver Cowdery’s letter to W.W. Phelps discussing early experiences and revelations in the formation of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.

Key Points:

  • Cowdery reflects on the passage of time and eternity.
  • Shares experiences traveling and facing challenges with Joseph Smith.
  • Describes the process of translating the Book of Mormon.
  • Mentions the lack of authority in other religions.
  • Recounts receiving the priesthood from an angel.
  • Expresses joy and certainty in their religious experiences.
  • Describes the spiritual impact of their revelations.
  • Plans to provide a full history of the church’s rise.

history.author: 길버트, 일라이
history.citation: Eli Gilbert - Oliver Cowdery, Oliver Cowdery, 1834. 후기 성도들의 메신저 및 옹호 (Kirtland, Ohio) 1, 아니오. 1 (1834년 10월):9-10쪽.
history.teaser:
A letter from Eli Gilbert to Oliver Cowdery discussing Gilbert’s personal loss, his interest in the Church, and his observations and opinions on religious matters in his community.

Key Points:

  • Gilbert’s sons were involved with the Church; one died from cholera.
  • Interest in the Book of Mormon and LDS teachings in Connecticut.
  • Gilbert read the Book of Mormon and found it corroborated the Bible.
  • Belief in the divine inspiration of the Book of Mormon.
  • Observations on local religious attitudes and prejudices.
  • Comments on the hardships faced by “Mormon” preachers and followers.
  • Discussion of local clergy and their compensation.
  • Queries about the lack of revelations in current publications.

history.author: 카우더리, 올리버
history.citation: 카우드리, 올리버. "편지 II." 후기 성도들의 메신저와 옹호자 (Kirtland, Ohio) 1, 아니오. 2 (1834년 11월):27-32쪽.
history.teaser:
Oliver Cowdery’s letter emphasizing the divine authority and continuity of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, paralleling its foundation to biblical precedents.

Key Points:

  • Cowdery promises a detailed history of the Latter Day Saints.
  • Emphasizes God’s works as clear, intelligible, and purposeful.
  • Draws parallels between the LDS Church and biblical narratives.
  • Argues the truth of the church is undeniable to honest seekers.
  • Claims pure religion withstands opposition and gains followers.
  • Notes the historical pattern of rejecting contemporary prophets.
  • Mentions the importance of judging by truth rather than rumor.
  • Intends to provide a narrative to inform and clarify the church’s history.

history.citation: 몰몬교가 비난했다. Painesville Telegraph (오하이오주 페인즈빌) (1834년 11월 28일).
history.teaser:
An advertisement for a book critical of Mormonism, providing a history and critique of the religion and its followers.

Key Points:

  • Book titled “Mormonism Unvailed” published in Painesville
  • Contains history of Mormonism from its rise to 1834
  • Includes peculiarities of the Mormon sect
  • 292 pages, 12 mo size
  • Available for sale at Painesville Telegraph office and book store
  • Merchants and booksellers can buy at reasonable terms

history.author: 스미스, 조셉, 1805-1844
history.citation: 조셉 스미스는 올리버 카우드리입니다. 후기 성도들의 메신저와 옹호자 (Kirtland, Ohio) 1, 아니오. 3 (1834년 12월):40쪽.
history.teaser:
A letter from Joseph Smith to Oliver Cowdery, discussing Smith’s early life and addressing accusations against his character.

Key Points:

  • Smith provides the time and place of his birth
  • Moved to Palmyra, N.Y. at the age of ten
  • Acknowledges youthful vices and follies
  • Denies gross violations of peace and good order
  • Regrets his former uncircumspect walk and unchaste conversation
  • Admits to acting against the precepts from God
  • Clarifies he is a man subject to passion
  • Requests the publication of his letter in the paper

history.citation: 올리버 카우드리와 W. W. 펠프스, 편지 번호. 3. 후기 성도들의 메신저와 옹호 (Kirtland, Ohio) 1, 아니오. 3 (1834년 12월):41-43쪽.
history.teaser:
Oliver Cowdery’s letter to W. W. Phelps discussing early challenges and spiritual inquiries faced by the LDS Church and its members.

Key Points:

  • Cowdery addresses the persecution faced by the LDS Church.
  • Emphasizes the importance of a correct account of events.
  • Mentions Joseph Smith’s early life and spiritual inquiries.
  • Describes religious excitement and division in Palmyra.
  • Joseph’s family’s religious affiliations influenced his reflections.
  • Joseph struggled with the idea of joining any existing church.
  • Highlights the confusion over which church was true.
  • Joseph sought a more certain understanding of God’s will.

history.citation: 몰몬교 기독교 등록 (보스턴) (보스턴) (12월 20일):76쪽. 12월 1834년 경 Sacket의 하버 택배에서 재판.
history.teaser:
An 1834 article from the Christian Register, originally from the Sacket’s Harbor Courier, detailing accusations against Joseph Smith and early Mormonism.

Key Points:

  • Joseph Smith described as a former county pauper and money digger
  • Smith claimed to have found golden plates, later named the Book of Mormon
  • Martin Harris provided financial support for Smith’s endeavors
  • Harris and Smith described as using deception in their activities
  • Martin Harris accused of domestic violence and hypocrisy
  • Smith and Harris characterized as untrustworthy by local community
  • Harris’s failed prophecies led to his diminished credibility
  • All Mormonites reportedly left the state of New York

history.author: 그리피스, 준 D.
history.citation: Griffiths, D., Jun. <i>오하이오, 북미의 새로운 정착촌에서 2 년 거주 : 이민자들에 대한 지시 사항, 132-41. 런던 : Westley와 Davis, 1835.
history.teaser:
An 1835 account by D. Griffiths, Jr. of his observations and understanding of Mormonism during his residence in Ohio, including its origins, beliefs, and practices.

Key Points:

  • Mormonism highlighted as a notable example of American religious enthusiasm
  • Angel’s revelation to Joseph Smith in 1829 introducing the Book of Mormon
  • Griffiths’ personal encounter with Mormon Elder and examination of Mormon texts
  • Description of the Book of Mormon’s content and claim of ancient origin
  • Testimony of eleven witnesses regarding the golden plates
  • Mormon practices include baptism by immersion and communal support
  • Mormons claim supernatural powers like healing and prophecy
  • Griffiths criticizes Mormonism’s credibility, citing its origins as a novel

history.author: 애브디, E.S. (에드워드 스트럿), 1791-1846
history.citation: ABDY, E. S. 미국 4 월, 1833년 10월, 1834년 4월, 3 : 40-41, 54-59까지의에서 10 월까지의 레지던스 및 투어 저널. 런던 : John Murray, 1835.
history.teaser:
E. S. Abdy’s observations on Mormonism and its followers during his travels in the United States.

Key Points:

  • Mormons or Mormonites had settled in the west, numbering around 5-6,000.
  • Joseph Smith published his “seal,” with six more revelations pending.
  • Mormons live in common, emphasizing equality and harmony.
  • They believe in the eventual ascendancy of Indians and blacks over whites.
  • 20,000 converts and 800 ministers by the time of writing.
  • Mormons face persecution due to their inclusive beliefs.
  • Joseph Smith’s work includes historical, prophetic, and didactic parts.
  • Mormon doctrines emphasize natural equality and non-discrimination.

history.document: 찬송가 63. P.M. 오, 멈춰봐, 붉은 남자
history.citation: o 멈추고, 빨간 사람에게 말해줘. <i>후자의 교회를위한 신성한 찬송가의 컬렉션, 83-84. Kirtland, Ohio : F. G. Williams & Company, 1835.
history.teaser:
A hymn from the original LDS hymnbook contemplating the origin and destiny of Native Americans in the context of LDS theology.

Key Points:

  • Questions the identity and lifestyle of Native Americans
  • Native person identifies as Ephraim, once blessed by Jacob
  • Discusses the fall of their ancestors into darkness
  • Describes the transition to a hunting lifestyle
  • Mentions a dwindling of their race and arts
  • Expresses hope for redemption and an end to oppression
  • Foresees a gathering and transformation of Native peoples
  • Anticipates joy and blessings through pure religion

history.citation: 몰몬성. J. Newton Brown 종교 지식의 백과 사전, 844. 보스턴 : Shattuck & Company, 1835. 십자가 및 침례식 저널에서 재판, 가을 1834 년 가을.
history.teaser:
An encyclopedia entry from 1835 providing a critical overview of the “Mormonites” and the origin of the Book of Mormon.

Key Points:

  • Mormonites believe in the Book of Mormon, comparing it to the Bible or Koran.
  • Joseph Smith found brass plates in Palmyra, NY, in 1826.
  • Smith interpreted the plates using a stone in his hat.
  • Disagreement with Martin Harris led to Oliver Cowdery’s involvement.
  • Smith claimed the Book of Mormon was a revelation from heaven.
  • Followers were persuaded to move to a New Zion in Missouri.
  • A weekly periodical disseminates new revelations among the community.
  • The Book of Mormon described as puerile eastern romance with no connection to sober history.

history.author: 사제 요시야, 1788-1851;
history.citation: 성직자, 요시야. 미국 고대, 79. 5th ed. 알바니 : 호프만과 화이트, 1835.
history.teaser:
A critique of the Book of Mormon and its origins by Josiah Priest, questioning the connection between Native Americans and the lost tribes of Israel.

Key Points:

  • Priest opposes the idea that the Ten Tribes were lost
  • Claims Ten Tribes are still in the east, near ancient Syria
  • Ridicules authors linking Indians to Jews as ignorant
  • Mentions the rise of the Mormonites and their golden book
  • Describes the Book of Mormon as a poor Old Testament imitation
  • Asserts the Book of Mormon lacks connection, object, or aim
  • Criticizes the Book’s language as too modern for an ancient text
  • Points out the Book of Mormon was written in Ontario County, NY

history.document: 찬송가 72. L. M. 혼돈으로부터 이 땅이 생겨나기 전에
history.citation: 카오스에서이 지구가 튀어 나오기 전에. 신성한 찬송가의 컬렉션, 후기 성도, 95-97. Kirtland, Ohio : F. G. Williams & Company, 1835.
history.teaser:

A hymn celebrating Joseph Smith’s role in restoring the gospel and translating the Book of Mormon.

  • Verse 2: Joseph Smith sought a better way in darkness

history.author: 프랫, 팔리 P. (팔리 파커), 1807-1857

  • Nephi’s journey to the promised land highlighted

An editorial review of E.D. Howe’s “Mormonism Unveiled,” criticizing Mormonism and endorsing Howe’s findings.

Oliver Cowdery defends the Book of Mormon and its teachings against criticisms in the Baptist publication “The Pioneer.”

  • Universalism prospering in Ohio despite other religious movements
  • Liberal Christianity seen as a natural fit for the region
  • Mormons added Egyptian mummies to their beliefs
  • Joseph Smith claims to interpret ancient manuscripts
  • Methodist clergyman in Newburg converts to Universalism
  • Five Universalist preachers active within thirty-five miles of the city
  • Call for more laborers to spread pure and undefiled religion
  • Advocates for religion based on love for God and humanity

history.author: 카우더리, 올리버
history.citation: 편지 VIII. 올리버 카우드리와 W. W. Phelps. 후기 성도들의 메신저와 옹호자 (Kirtland, Ohio) 2, 아니오. 1 (10 월 1835):195-202쪽.
history.teaser:
A detailed letter from Oliver Cowdery to W. W. Phelps discussing the circumstances and divine experiences surrounding the discovery and translation of the Book of Mormon.

Key Points:

  • Cowdery describes the location and deposit of the Book of Mormon plates.
  • Mentions divine instructions and reflections on holy grounds.
  • Details on how the plates were protected and preserved for centuries.
  • Joseph Smith’s initial failures to obtain the plates due to lack of obedience.
  • Divine manifestations and instruction on the importance of purity and obedience.
  • Joseph Smith’s character and the unjust slander he faced are defended.
  • References to divine guidance and prophecies concerning the Book of Mormon.
  • Emphasizes the sacredness and divine purpose of the Book of Mormon.

history.author: 펠프스, 윌리엄 와인, 1792-1872
history.citation: 편지 번호 11. W. W. Phelps ~ 올리버 카우드리. 후기 성도들의 메신저와 옹호 (Kirtland, Ohio) 2, 아니오. 1 (1835년 10월):193-95쪽.
history.teaser:
W. W. Phelps writes to Oliver Cowdery, discussing the Book of Mormon’s implications for Native Americans and their identification as descendants of Israelites.

Key Points:

  • Phelps connects the Book of Mormon to the history of Native Americans.
  • Describes Native Americans as remnants of Israel, deserving of the gospel.
  • Expresses joy over the prospect of Native Americans’ salvation.
  • Views the Book of Mormon as a key tool for Native American redemption.
  • Phelps is optimistic about Native Americans becoming a “white and delightsome people.”
  • Considers the global population and hypothesizes about hidden tribes of Israel.
  • Criticizes contemporary Christianity for lacking faith and miracles.
  • Encourages the Latter Day Saints to keep faith for miracles and blessings.

history.author: 카우더리, 올리버
history.citation: 카우드리, 올리버. "니파이인의 기록." 후기 성도들의 메신저와 옹호자 (Kirtland, Ohio) 2, 아니오. 1 (10 월 1835):203-4쪽.
history.teaser:
A letter by Oliver Cowdery reflecting on the journey and impact of the Book of Mormon since its revelation to Joseph Smith Jr. in 1827.

Key Points:

  • The angel of the Lord delivered the record of the Nephites in 1827
  • Thousands have heard its contents since its translation
  • The Book has been translated and printed despite opposition
  • Elders have been sent throughout the US and to Canada
  • The message has been proclaimed successfully against opposition
  • The church’s influence is reaching Europe
  • Call for saints to prepare for gathering and redemption
  • The church has grown significantly in eight years

history.author: 펠프스, 윌리엄 와인, 1792-1872
history.citation: 편지 번호 12. W. W. Phelps ~ 올리버 카우드리. 후기 성도들의 메신저와 옹호 (Kirtland, Ohio) 2, 아니오. 2 (1835년 11월):221-23쪽.
history.teaser:
A letter from W. W. Phelps to Oliver Cowdery discussing the significance of Cumorah and the message of the angel to Joseph Smith.

Key Points:

  • Phelps sees Cumorah as significant as Sinai to Latter Day Saints
  • Cumorah, a monument of marvelous works and a sacred depository
  • Discussion on the loss and wickedness of ancient peoples there
  • Angel’s message to Joseph Smith emphasized obedience to God
  • Pattern given by the angel as a guide to discern spirits
  • Book of Mormon seen as a cause of world commotion
  • Comparison to the finding of the book of the law by Hilkiah
  • Call for righteousness and rejection of false teachings

history.author: 스캐릿, 아이작
history.citation: 후기 성도들. Isaac Scarritt 씨 H, 1835년 7월 13일. 서양식 기독교 옹호 (신시내티, 오하이오) 2, 아니오. 30 (1835년 11월 20일):120쪽.
history.teaser:
A letter by Isaac Scarritt, expressing his criticisms and doubts about the teachings and interpretations of the Latter Day Saints, published in the Western Christian Advocate.

Key Points:

  • Scarritt examined Latter Day Saints’ beliefs but remained unconvinced.
  • He criticizes the division of scriptural testimony between Judah and Joseph.
  • Questions the interpretation of Ezekiel’s sticks as scriptures.
  • Challenges the claim of Ephraimites in America and the historicity of the Book of Mormon.
  • Points out contradictions between the Book of Mormon and the Bible.
  • Criticizes the interpretation of Isaiah’s prophecy by Latter Day Saints.
  • Rejects the idea that translators of scriptures need to be divinely inspired.
  • Accuses the Latter Day Saints of detracting from the authenticity of the Bible.

history.author: 스미스, 조셉, 1805-1844
history.citation: 스미스, 요셉, 주니어 "후기 성도 교회의 ​​장로들에게." 후반의 날 성도의 메신저와 옹호자 (Kirtland, Ohio) 2, 아니오. 3 (12 월 1835):227-28쪽.
history.teaser:
A letter by Joseph Smith, Jr. to the elders of the Church, reflecting on the Book of Mormon’s significance and addressing opposition.

Key Points:

  • Comparison of the Book of Mormon to a mustard seed
  • Book of Mormon described as truth sprouting from the earth
  • God’s powers, gifts, and angels are lodging in its branches
  • Church likened to an impenetrable rock amidst opposition
  • Mentions opposition by referencing “Mormonism Unveiled”
  • Addresses critics and their tactics of falsehood
  • Mentions legal troubles of anti-Mormon author P. Hurlburt
  • Addresses disbelief and bias against Mormons

history.citation: 너는 거짓말하지 않아. W.와 펠프스는 존 휘트머에게. 후기 성도들의 메신저와 옹호 (Kirtland, Ohio) 2, 아니오. 3 (12 월 1835년 12월):230-33쪽.
history.teaser:
An open letter from W. W. Phelps to John Whitmer discussing the persecution of the Latter Day Saints and defending their actions and beliefs against public slander.

Key Points:

  • W. W. Phelps addresses the public’s misunderstanding of the LDS Church
  • Phelps argues against the idea that the LDS members should not defend themselves
  • Discusses the misrepresentation and lies spread about the Church
  • Refutes false reports of a Mormon preacher’s tragical event
  • Criticizes the media for spreading falsehoods about the Church
  • Describes the persecution and challenges faced by the LDS Church
  • Phelps calls for repentance from those who have slandered the Church
  • Emphasizes the Church’s pursuit of truth and defense against falsehood

history.author: M.A.H.
history.citation: M., A. H. "고대와 현대 몰몬교" Western Examiner (세인트 루이스, 미주리) 2, 아니오. 46 (12월 10일 10 일):366-67쪽.
history.teaser:
An article from the Western Examiner comparing ancient and modern Mormonism, heavily critiquing the foundations and followers of the Latter Day Saint movement as an imposition on common sense.

Key Points:

  • Article criticizes the acceptance of Mormonism among people.
  • Leaders and followers of Mormonism described as societal dregs.
  • Comparison between ancient and modern revelations.
  • Claims both ancient and modern founders were impostors.
  • Mentions other religious texts as similar impositions.
  • Discusses human nature’s predisposition to believe in the marvelous.
  • Warns of the long-term impact of not refuting Mormon claims.
  • Calls for contemporary testimony to prevent future deceptions.

history.author: Stors, Richard S. (리처드 솔터), 1787-1873
history.citation: Storrs, Richard. Rev. Samuel Green, 129-39의 회고록. 보스턴 : 퍼킨스 & 마빈, 1836.
history.teaser:
A memoir containing a letter by Rev. Samuel Green expressing his concerns and warnings about the allure of Mormonism to a member of his congregation.

Key Points:

  • Rev. Green expresses vigilance and tenderness for his flock.
  • Warns against the delusions of Mormonism leading to perdition.
  • Emphasizes the importance of adhering to the teachings of the Bible.
  • Advises testing every spirit to see if it is from God.
  • Stresses that new revelations must be accompanied by clear miraculous proof.
  • Warns against accepting any teachings that go beyond the Bible.
  • Discusses the integrity and completeness of the Biblical canon.
  • Urges return to the “old paths” and good way of traditional Christian faith.

history.author: 헤이워드, 존
history.citation: 헤이워드, 존. <i>미국 및 영국 성의 모든 기독교 교단의 종교적 신조와 통계, 유대인, 아메리칸 인디언, 신청사, 마하 미터의 종교적 감정에 대한 설명과 함께 있습니다. 알파벳 순으로 배열, 132-38. 보스턴 : John Hayward, 1836.
history.teaser:
An 1836 analysis by John Hayward of the Book of Mormon, its content, structure, and the narrative it presents.

Key Points:

  • Book of Mormon contains 588 pages and several books.
  • Lehi’s journey from Jerusalem to the Americas is detailed.
  • Nephi retrieves records on plates of brass.
  • Lehi’s descendants split into Nephites and Lamanites.
  • Nephites practiced Christianity before Christ’s birth.
  • Jesus Christ visits the Americas after his resurrection.
  • Book of Ether recounts the Jaredites from the Tower of Babel.
  • Moroni concludes the record, promising spiritual gifts.

history.author: 펠프스, W. W.
history.citation: 펠프스, W. W. "인디언들." 후기 성도들의 메신저와 옹호자 (Kirtland, Ohio) 2, 아니오. 4 (1836년 1월):245-48쪽.
history.teaser:
An article by W.W. Phelps discussing the LDS Church’s perspective on Native Americans and their role in the gathering of Israel, in light of U.S. government policies on Indian removal.

Key Points:

  • Gathering of Israel is a core belief of the LDS Church
  • Scripture guides the gathering of the elect from all nations
  • Book of Mormon identifies Native Americans as part of Israel
  • U.S. government relocating Indians to lands west of Mississippi
  • Removal plan aims to improve and protect Native Americans
  • Extensive territories allocated to various tribes
  • Arrangements include support for physical comfort and moral improvement
  • LDS view gathering of Native Americans as fulfilling prophecy

history.citation: 망상을 조심하십시오! 후기 성도들의 메신저와 옹호자 (Kirtland, Ohio) 2, 아니오. 4 (1836년 1월):250-52쪽.
history.teaser:
An article from the “Latter Day Saints’ Messenger and Advocate” defending the LDS faith against accusations of delusion and emphasizing the manifestation of spiritual gifts as evidence of its truth.

Key Points:

  • Article addresses concerns about being deluded by Mormonism
  • Questions the foundation of Protestant beliefs
  • Points to the absence of miraculous signs in other denominations
  • Highlights the presence of spiritual gifts among the Mormons
  • Warns against the materialistic values of the Protestant community
  • Mentions the Book of Mormon as a guide to happiness and truth
  • Emphasizes the importance of spiritual signs as evidence of faith
  • Discusses the slow progression of the Latter Day Saints in acquiring spiritual gifts

history.author: 엔슬리, 에브라임
history.citation: Ephraim Ensley 형제 Badger, 1835, Reading, New York. Christian Palladium (Unionmills, New York) 4, 아니오. 18 (1836년 1월 15일):280쪽.
history.teaser:
A letter expressing skepticism towards the authenticity of the Book of Mormon, contrasting its teachings with traditional Christian beliefs.

Key Points:

  • Mormon Preachers active in Reading, New York
  • Attempt to prove the Book of Mormon as the stick of Joseph
  • Ephraim Ensley borrowed and examined the Book of Mormon critically
  • Ensley found the book to be a farce
  • Critiques the Book of Mormon’s stance on infant baptism
  • Questions the historical and theological consistency of the Book of Mormon
  • Compares Mormon teachings unfavorably with traditional Christian views
  • Expresses hope that God saves the land from deception

history.author: 바, 올리버
history.citation: Olion [Oliver] Barr to Ebenezer Barr, 1835년 9월 22일. 후기 성도들 ‘ 메신저와 옹호 (Kirtland, Ohio) 2, 아니오. 5 (2 월 1836):257-58쪽.
history.teaser:
A letter by Oliver Barr expressing skepticism towards the claims of Mormonism and emphasizing the completeness of the Gospel as delivered by Jesus Christ and the apostles.

Key Points:

  • Salvation plan devised in heaven and revealed through revelation
  • Revelation made to chosen individuals, not directly to everyone
  • Miracles are evidence of divine authorization of revelations
  • Moses, Jesus Christ, and Apostles confirmed their teachings with miracles
  • Once the Gospel was fully revealed, miracles ceased
  • Questioning the need for new revelations or miracles
  • Belief that the entire Gospel was delivered by the apostles
  • Open to being corrected if his objections to Mormonism can be answered

history.author: 1853년 올리버 바
history.citation: Oliver Barr to Sidney Rigdon, 2월 29일 2966. 후기 성도들의 메신저와 옹호 (Kirtland, Ohio) 2, 아니오. 6 (3 월 1836):273쪽.
history.teaser:
A letter from Oliver Barr to Sidney Rigdon expressing curiosity and skepticism about the teachings of the LDS Church.

Key Points:

  • Barr received Rigdon’s letter and examined it impartially.
  • Emphasizes the importance of understanding cardinal points of religion.
  • Acknowledges the kind spirit of Rigdon’s correspondence.
  • Expresses curiosity about Rigdon’s claim that the original Gospel has disappeared.
  • Asks specific questions about the nature and whereabouts of the Gospel.
  • Queries if the Mormons possess the complete Gospel.
  • Seeks candid responses to satisfy his inquiring mind.
  • Desires that their correspondence will glorify God and benefit them both.

history.author: 휘트머, 존
history.citation: 휘트메르, 존. "주소." 후기 성도들의 메신저와 옹호자 (Kirtland, Ohio) 2, 아니오. 6 (3 월 1836):286-88쪽.
history.teaser:
John Whitmer expresses his reflections and testimonies concerning the early days of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints and his role in its publication efforts.

Key Points:

  • Whitmer praises Oliver Cowdery’s character and leadership.
  • Highlights the responsibility and humility of an editor.
  • Emphasizes the power of preaching and God’s choice of simple means to confound the wise.
  • Reflects on living in a time when God is working for the good of His covenant people.
  • Testifies of the authenticity of the Book of Mormon and Joseph Smith’s prophetic role.
  • Emphasizes the importance of living by all of God’s revealed words.
  • Encourages elders to promote the Messenger and Advocate for the welfare of humanity.
  • Urges continued revelation and guidance by the Holy Spirit for truth.

history.author: 시드니 릭던, 1793-1876
history.citation: Sidney Rigdon to Oliver Barr, 3 월 1836. 후기 성도들의 메신저와 옹호 (Kirtland, Ohio) 2, 아니오. 6 (3 월 1836):273-74쪽.
history.teaser:
A letter from Sidney Rigdon explaining the gospel and its manifestations according to New Testament teachings, and asserting the restoration of these gifts in the Latter Day Saint movement.

Key Points:

  • Rigdon addresses questions about the nature of the gospel.
  • Defines the gospel as God’s power to save, made known in the New Testament.
  • Emphasizes the importance of receiving the Holy Spirit’s gifts.
  • Mentions specific spiritual gifts: speaking in tongues, prophecy, healing.
  • Asserts that the gospel includes a specific order of church offices.
  • Claims this gospel order had disappeared but has been restored.
  • Indicates that the power of God is received through ordained ministry.
  • Asserts the restoration of the gospel through divine revelation and messengers.

history.author: 하이드, 오슨, 1805-1878
history.citation: Orson Hyde 편집자에게. 후기 성도들의 메신저와 옹호자 (Kirtland, Ohio) 2, 아니오. 7 (1836년 4월):296쪽.
history.teaser:
Orson Hyde reports on his missionary work and reflects on the opposition faced by the LDS Church.

Key Points:

  • Orson Hyde returns from a three-week mission in Portage, Ohio.
  • Preached in Hiram, where Joseph Smith Jr. and Sidney Rigdon were attacked.
  • Despite past violence, some in Hiram are embracing the truth.
  • Hyde baptized eight people in Mantua, Shalersville, and Middlebury.
  • Mentions the potential for further missionary work in the area.
  • Reflects on the resilience of the LDS Church against opposition.
  • Names A. Campbell, E. Booth, and E.D. Howe as notable opponents.
  • Asserts that opposition writings have failed to hinder the church’s progress.

history.author: 엘스, 제임스 H.
history.citation: James H. Eells, Joshua Leavitt, 1836년 4월 1일 뉴욕 전도자 (뉴욕) 7, 아니오. 15 (4월 9일 9 일):59쪽.
history.teaser:
A letter to the editor of the New York Evangelist by James H. Eells, discussing the rise of Mormonism and comparing it to Islam.

Key Points:

  • Mormonism compared to the rise of Islam
  • Mormons seen as a significant and growing religious sect
  • Description of the Kirtland Temple and its unique features
  • Mormons eager for education, including Hebrew studies
  • Mormons profess high levels of piety and devotion
  • Only Joseph Smith authorized to commit revelations to writing
  • Book of Mormon criticized for lacking literary quality
  • Mormons believed to be sincere but deluded by their faith

history.author: 프랫, 팔리 P. (팔리 파커), 1807-1857
history.citation: Parley P. Pratt to Oliver Cowdery, Oliver Cowdery, 26556. 후기 성도들의 메신저와 옹호 (Kirtland, Ohio) 2, 아니오. 8 (5 월 1836) : 3 18-20.
history.teaser:
A letter by Parley P. Pratt detailing his missionary experiences in Upper Canada, challenges faced, and his defense of the Book of Mormon against criticisms.

Key Points:

  • Pratt’s mission in Upper Canada with Elders O. Pratt and F. Nickerson
  • Difficulties in finding public spaces for preaching, leading to outdoor events
  • Encounters with clergy attempting to discredit the Book of Mormon
  • Rebuttal of criticisms regarding anachronisms and moral actions in the Book of Mormon
  • Comparison of criticisms of the Book of Mormon to the Bible
  • Public debate with Rev. Mr. Milkins and Pratt’s defense of Book of Mormon
  • Baptism of new believers following Pratt’s preaching and debates
  • Growth of the Church in Upper Canada as a result of missionary work

history.author: 시드니 릭던, 1793-1876
history.citation: 시드니 장비 올리버 카우드리에. 후기 성도들의 메신저와 옹호자 (Kirtland, Ohio) 2, 아니오. 9 (6 월 1836):334-35쪽.
history.teaser:
A letter from Sidney Rigdon to Oliver Cowdery discussing legal threats from Simons Rider and proposing a humorous solution.

Key Points:

  • Rigdon discusses being threatened with a lawsuit by Simons Rider
  • Rigdon pleads publicly with Rider not to sue him
  • Mentions the truth as a tight fit for Rider, causing discomfort
  • Proposes a humorous solution involving Rigdon’s wealthy uncle
  • Adamson Bentley suggested as a partner for Rider’s scheme
  • Bentley is accused of profiting from others’ property before
  • Rigdon suggests this scheme might prevent the lawsuit
  • Also mentions Darwin Atwater and Howe’s book in relation to Campbellism

history.author: 1853년 올리버 바
history.citation: 올리버 바르 시트 티 롱 돈. 후기 성도들의 메신저와 옹호자 (Kirtland, Ohio) 2, 아니오. 9 (6 월 1836):321-25쪽.
history.teaser:
A letter from Oliver Barr to Sidney Rigdon discussing the nature of revelation, miracles, and the gospel according to the early Latter Day Saint movement.

Key Points:

  • Barr argues revelation and miracles were foundational to early Christian doctrine.
  • Disputes Rigdon’s views on the necessity of ongoing revelation and miracles.
  • Asserts that the New Testament contains the full plan of salvation.
  • Challenges the idea that modern revelation and miracles are needed.
  • Questions the LDS claim of a departed and restored gospel.
  • Argues for a return to the original gospel, not a new revelation.
  • Discusses the role of miracles in confirming the message of prophets.
  • Emphasizes the sufficiency of the New Testament for salvation.

history.author: 시드니 릭던, 1793-1876
history.citation: Sidney Rigdon ~ Oliver Barr, Oliver Barr, 11월 15일 1536. 후기 성도들의 메신저와 옹호 (Kirtland, Ohio) 2, 아니오. 5 (2 월 1836):258-63쪽.
history.teaser:
A detailed letter from Sidney Rigdon discussing the nature of revelation, miracles, and the consistency of the gospel.

Key Points:

  • Revelation results from faith and presupposes belief in God.
  • Revelations are not solely based on the veracity of prophets.
  • Miracles are not the only proof of divine revelation.
  • Miracles were signs for believers, not exclusively for apostles.
  • Modern preaching lacks the power and authority of ancient gospel.
  • The absence of miracles in modern churches questions their authenticity.
  • The gospel’s effects differed greatly between ancient and modern times.
  • Restoration of the original gospel requires revelation from God.

history.author: 시드니 릭던, 1793-1876
history.citation: Sidney Rigdon to Oliver Barr, Oliver Barr, 1836. 후기 성도들의 메신저와 옹호자 (Kirtland, Ohio) 2, 아니오. 9 (6 월 1836):326-29쪽.
history.teaser:
A letter from Sidney Rigdon to Oliver Barr discussing the nature and necessity of revelation and miracles in the context of the Restoration movement.

Key Points:

  • Rigdon argues that faith precedes revelation.
  • Asserts that man cannot depend on others for knowledge of salvation.
  • Challenges the notion that miracles are the only proof of divine revelation.
  • Emphasizes that the Spirit can testify to the truth of revelations.
  • Questions the discontinuation of miracles in modern Christianity.
  • Highlights differences between ancient and modern gospel effects.
  • Argues for the restoration of the gospel through revelation.
  • Invites Barr to further discuss and explore these theological points.

history.citation: 몰몬교 웨인 센티넬 (팔미라, 뉴욕) (1836년 6월 17일).
history.teaser:
A letter critiquing the Latter Day Saint movement’s claims about ongoing revelation and miracles.

Key Points:

  • Letter addresses the necessity of revelation and miracles.
  • Argues that revelation was necessary for initial faith in God.
  • Emphasizes that miracles confirmed the message of God’s messengers.
  • Claims the gospel is fully revealed and recorded in the New Testament.
  • Argues that no more revelation or miracles are needed today.
  • Asserts the gospel has not disappeared, refuting the need for restoration.
  • Urges the world to return to the gospel, not for the gospel to be restored.
  • Requests that the correspondence be published in full.

history.author: 캠벨, 알렉산더, 1788-1866
history.citation: 캠벨, 알렉산더. "경전의 영감". 밀레니그 기념일 하이너 7, 아니오. 8 (8 월 1836):347쪽.
history.teaser:
A critique of religious movements, including Mormonism, by Alexander Campbell, highlighting perceived commonalities in their methods of attracting followers.

Key Points:

  • Campbell discusses how impostors manipulate desires for knowledge.
  • Mormonism is criticized for ministering to curiosity with the Book of Mormon.
  • Claims of miraculous power and mysterious visions are tactics used.
  • Comparison made with Islam and its promises of knowledge and paradise.
  • Mormonism’s appeal includes tales of the lost tribes of Israel and origins of Native Americans.
  • Mormonism’s methods likened to other religious movements’ use of novelties and visions.
  • Article implies the danger of forsaking duty for curiosity’s gratification.
  • Campbell aims to expose similarities between Mormonism and other deemed impostures.

history.citation: 몰몬교 - 그 역사. 필라델피아 거울 (8월 22일 2266년 8월 22일).
history.teaser:
An article from the Philadelphia Mirror discussing the origins of Mormonism and the theory that it was derived from Solomon Spalding’s manuscript.

Key Points:

  • Article suggests Mormonism originated from Solomon Spalding’s work
  • Spalding was educated and ordained but left the ministry
  • Spalding wrote a historical novel, “Manuscript Found”
  • “Manuscript Found” is claimed to be the basis of the Book of Mormon
  • Describes a journey from Jerusalem to America, forming civilizations
  • Spalding’s manuscript explained as accounting for Native American ancestors
  • After Spalding’s death, Sidney Rigdon allegedly acquired the manuscript
  • Joseph Smith published the Book of Mormon, claimed as divine revelation

history.author: 코, 트루먼
history.citation: Coe, Truman. "몰몬교" 신시내티 저널과 서부 구리 (8월 25일 2566). 오하이오 옵저버에서 재 인쇄, 8월 1836년 경
history.teaser:
An early critique of Mormonism by Truman Coe, expressing skepticism about its origins and practices.

Key Points:

history.citation: 몰몬경 성경 기독교 등록기와 보스턴 관찰자 (보스톤, 매사추세츠) 18, 아니오. 970 (4월 4일 1839).
history.teaser:
An article from a Boston newspaper discussing the origins of the Book of Mormon, suggesting it’s a product of both a cultivated mind and gross superstition.

Key Points:

  • Article from the Boston Recorder discusses the Mormon Bible’s origin
  • Book seen as a mix of cultivated production and gross superstition
  • Narrative procured by Rev. Mr. Stow, who encountered Mormonism
  • Stow’s experiences suggest he’s witnessed Mormonism’s “grossest forms”

history.author: c
history.citation: C. "등록 및 관찰자의 경우." 기독교 등록기 및 보스턴 관찰자 (보스톤) 18, 아니오. 971 (11월 11일 11 일).
history.teaser:
An 1839 article questioning the origins of the Book of Mormon and the legitimacy of the claims made by Matilda Davison regarding its connection to her late husband Solomon Spaulding’s manuscript.

Key Points:

  • Mormonism described as speculative and rapidly adopted
  • Mormons portrayed as victims of persecution
  • Question raised about the origin of the Mormon Bible
  • Matilda Davison’s letter suggests a connection to Spaulding’s manuscript
  • Article questions the proof of Davison’s claims
  • Public unaware if the Spaulding manuscript was compared to the Book of Mormon
  • Questions why Mormons continue to grow despite controversy
  • Author seeks answers for personal and public clarification

history.citation: 몰몬경 성경 트럼펫과 유니버설 주의자 잡지 (보스톤) 11, 아니오. 48 (1839년 5월 18일).
history.teaser:
An article suggesting the Book of Mormon originated from a manuscript written by Solomon Spaulding for entertainment.

Key Points:

  • Claims the Book of Mormon was originally a historical romance
  • Attributed to Solomon Spaulding, a Dartmouth College graduate
  • Linked to mounds and forts along the Ohio River
  • Friends of Spaulding recognized passages when a Mormon preacher visited
  • Original manuscript found among Spaulding’s papers
  • Spaulding considered printing the work
  • Manuscript left at a printing office where Sidney Rigdon worked
  • Implies Rigdon copied the manuscript, linking it to Mormonism

history.citation: 몰몬교 Alton Telegraph (Alton, Illinois) 4, 아니오. 22 (5월 25일 1839).
history.teaser:
An article discussing the arrival of Mormons in Illinois, their beliefs, and the debated origins of the Book of Mormon.

Key Points:

  • Mormons have recently arrived in Illinois
  • They may attempt to make a permanent settlement
  • Book of Mormon considered a direct revelation by Mormons
  • Rest of the world generally views it as an imposture
  • Mrs. Davison’s statement on the book’s origin mentioned
  • Authenticity of Davison’s statement supported by reputable names
  • Article advocates for universal toleration and respect for beliefs
  • Mormons have the right to worship as they see fit under the Constitution

history.citation: 몰몬교의 기원 Atkinson의 저녁 우편 및 필라델피아 토요일 뉴스 (필라델피아) 18 (5월 18399일).
history.teaser:
An 1839 newspaper article proposing that the Book of Mormon derived from a manuscript by Solomon Spaulding.

Key Points:

  • Book of Mormon linked to Solomon Spaulding’s manuscript
  • Spaulding created an “historical romance” about ancient mounds
  • Manuscript fell into the hands of Sidney Rigdon, per the claim
  • Spaulding’s work recognized by residents of New Salem as similar to Book of Mormon
  • Widow of Spaulding aimed to expose the Book of Mormon’s origins
  • 1834 effort to compare Spaulding’s manuscript with the Book of Mormon
  • Spaulding’s widow describes the misappropriation of his work as delusion
  • Testimony of Spaulding’s widow presented as credible and earnest

history.author: 캠벨, 알렉산더, 1788-1866
history.citation: 캠벨, 알렉산더. "몰몬경 성경" 밀레니그어 쩌둥 열매 3, no. 6 (6 월 1839):267-68쪽.
history.teaser:
A critique by Alexander Campbell, attributing the creation of the Book of Mormon to Sidney Rigdon and suggesting it was based on Solomon Spaulding’s manuscript.

Key Points:

  • Campbell doubts the divine origin of the Book of Mormon
  • Identifies Sidney Rigdon as the “leading conjuror” behind it
  • Mentions Solomon Spaulding’s manuscript as the basis of the Book of Mormon
  • Believes that Spaulding’s widow could provide information on the subject
  • Urges widespread dissemination of this information
  • Comments on the gullibility of the generation
  • Links ignorance of the Bible to susceptibility to delusion

history.teaser:
An article from the Alton Telegraph discussing claims that the Book of Mormon was derived from a manuscript written by Solomon Spalding, challenging its divine origin.

  • Matilda Davison claims Book of Mormon derived from Solomon Spalding’s work
  • Spalding wrote the manuscript 26 years earlier due to illness
  • Claims challenge the Book of Mormon’s divine origin
  • Mormonism Unveiled by G.D. Howe corroborates Davison’s statement
  • John Spalding and others recognize parts of the Book of Mormon from Spalding’s manuscript
  • Names and incidents in the Book of Mormon recalled by Spalding’s acquaintances

history.author: 슈리글리, J.
history.citation: Shrigley, J. "몰몬교" 복음주의 잡지와 복음 옹호 (Utica, New York) 10, 아니오. 23 (1839년 6월 7일):182쪽.
history.teaser:
A letter questioning the consistency of Mormon beliefs on universal happiness with a passage from the Book of Mormon.

Key Points:

  • Letter addresses Rev. S. P. Landers about Mormons.
  • Mormons believe in eventual happiness in one of three heavens.
  • Question raised on how this belief aligns with Book of Mormon’s teachings.
  • Specific passage from “Book of Maroni” questions universal happiness.
  • Passage mentions danger of death, hell, and endless torment.
  • Seeking clarification on the teachings of the Mormon Bible.

history.author: 시드니 릭던, 1793-1876

Sidney Rigdon’s letter to the editor refuting allegations about the Book of Mormon’s origin related to Solomon Spalding.

Key Points:

  • Refutes the story connecting the Book of Mormon to Spalding’s writings
  • Claims never to have been involved with a printing office owned by Patterson in Pittsburgh

  • Accuses Hurlburt and associates of fabricating lies against the LDS Church
