  • Believes accusations are aimed at preventing public investigation of the truth
  • Views the attacks as a testament to the strength of his and the church’s position

history.author: D., B.
history.citation: D., B. "몰몬교" 피오리아 레지스터와 노스 웨스턴 지표 (피오리아, 일리노이) 3, 아니오. 13 (1839년 6월 29일).
history.teaser:
An 1839 article defending Mormonism and its scriptures against accusations and presenting a witness testimony.

Key Points:

  • Mormons do not replace the Bible with the Book of Mormon
  • Criticizes the narrative connecting Spaulding’s manuscript to the Book of Mormon
  • Denies the authorization of women preachers in LDS Church
  • Highlights contradictions in accusations against the Book of Mormon’s origin
  • Testimony of P. P. Pratt on his conversion and the truth of the Book of Mormon

  • Refutes the Spaulding theory for the Book of Mormon’s origin
  • Urges repentance and baptism for the remission of sins

history.author: 패튼, W.

A letter to the editor responding critically to S. Rigdon’s previous article, defending the community’s integrity against accusations of dishonesty related to their views on Mormonism.

Key Points:

  • Patten criticizes Rigdon’s lack of candor and decorum
  • Rigdon’s writing suggests all opposed to Mormonism are “liars”
  • Western people welcomed Mormons, contradicting Rigdon’s claims
  • Rigdon’s article is seen as disrespectful and dishonest
  • Rigdon claims special divine mission, compared unfavorably with gospel
  • Patten provides evidence of Rigdon’s dishonesty
  • Rigdon’s perversion of “her testimony” highlighted as a lie
  • Patten challenges Rigdon’s accusations with specific questions

history.author: 스콧, 월터
history.citation: Scott, Walter. "몰몬경 성경" 전도자 (카르타고, 오하이오) 7, 아니오. 7 (7월 1일 1839):160-61쪽.

A critical examination of Mormonism and its early influence in Ohio by Walter Scott, focusing on Sidney Rigdon’s role.

history.author: 돕슨, 벤자민

A letter by Benjamin Dobson commenting on Mormon meetings and the general perception of Mormons in 1839.

  • Mormon preacher aimed to validate the Book of Mormon with the Bible
  • Debate followed the sermon, questioning Mormon beliefs

history.author: 셰털리, H.R.

An early non-Mormon perspective on Latter-day Saint beliefs and practices, highlighting doctrinal interpretations and prophecies.

  • Mormons interpret the Bible literally
  • Belief in temporary hell until the first resurrection
  • Three heavens: Telestial, Terrestrial, Celestial

history.author: 지혼, J.H.

A critical examination of Mormon beliefs and practices by J. H. Gihon, highlighting inconsistencies and questioning the sincerity of Mormon preachers.

Key Points:

  • Article questions the sincerity and Restorationist claims of Mormons.
  • Mormon Bible considered blasphemous and absurd by the author.
  • Claims of eternal damnation for non-believers criticized.
  • Mormon faith described as shifting to match audience beliefs.
  • Mormon preachers accused of insincerity and deception.
  • Mormons seen as Partialists, exclusive and bigoted.
  • Author warns against associating too closely with Mormons.
  • Encourages caution until Mormons reject the Book of Mormon.

history.author: 바들람, 알렉산더
history.citation: Badlam, 알렉산더. "교활한 장치가 감지되었습니다." Quincy Whig (Quincy, 일리노이 주) 2, 아니오. 29 (1839년 11월 16일)

An article refuting claims about the origin of the Book of Mormon, specifically addressing accusations of plagiarism.

Key Points:

  • Article addresses rumors about the Book of Mormon’s origin
  • John Haven’s letter to his daughter disputes these claims
  • Mrs. Davidson denies writing or seeing the letter in question
  • D. R. Austin accused of misrepresenting Mrs. Davidson’s words
  • Mrs. Davidson confirms some similarity in names but not content

A letter detailing a series of LDS meetings in New Jersey, showcasing the early missionary efforts and community response.

Key Points:

  • Woods meeting commenced with singing, prayer, and preaching
  • Oliver Granger and others addressed the congregation
  • Unanimous vote on missionary assignments in Pennsylvania and New Jersey
  • Two individuals presented themselves for baptism
  • Large congregation of up to three thousand people gathered
  • Elders testified about the Book of Mormon and spiritual experiences
  • $30 collected for the persecuted Brethren in Missouri
  • Eight baptisms conducted with more prospects

A detailed rebuttal of the Spaulding theory for the origin of the Book of Mormon, asserting the narrative as a fabrication.

  • Claims against the Book of Mormon’s divine origin are called fabrications.
  • Dr. P. Hurlbert is identified as the originator of the Spaulding theory.

  • Discrepancies in the Spaulding story are highlighted to discredit it.

  • Winchester affirms his faith in the Book of Mormon despite the Spaulding story.

A pamphlet warning against Mormonism, critiquing its founder Joseph Smith, its teachings, and comparing its claims to traditional Christian doctrine.

Key Points:

  • Questions the legitimacy of Mormonite messengers as true messengers of God.
  • Discusses Joseph Smith’s history and claims of finding the Book of Mormon.
  • Describes the rise of Nauvoo and Smith’s eventual death.
  • Compares Mormonite doctrine with biblical scripture.

  • Refutes Heys’ reliance on discredited American newspaper stories.
  • Emphasizes argument with scripture, not stories or rumors.
  • Compares conflicting accounts of the Book of Mormon’s origin.
  • Criticizes Heys and Livesey for contradicting testimonies.
  • Advises Heys to adhere to truth and scriptural proof.
  • Reminds of past Methodist persecution, parallels to Mormon experience.
  • Open to public discussion on Book of Mormon, with scripture as the test.

history.author: 프랫, 팔리 P. (팔리 파커), 1807-1857

Parley P. Pratt’s defense against accusations and critiques of Mormonism by Thomas Taylor and Richard Livesey, emphasizing the authenticity of the LDS faith’s doctrines and practices.

  • Asserts gifts of the Holy Spirit are not to be exhibited as curiosities.
  • Emphasizes that faith comes by hearing the word of God, not signs.
  • Denies allegations made in opponents’ publications as false.
  • Claims Book of Mormon is supported by prophecy fulfillment.
  • Compares Latter-Day Saints’ persecution with that of early Christians.
  • Defends the use of money in religion for holy purposes.
  • Outlines what constitutes the church of Christ and the gospel.

  • Claims Book of Mormon is a deception
  • Origins of the Book of Mormon linked to Solomon Spaulding

history.citation: Morrish, W. J. 후기 성도와 몰몬경. 장관의 두 번째 경고, 1-4. Ledbury : J. Gibbs, 1840.
history.teaser:
A critical pamphlet by W. J. Morrish warning his congregation against the teachings and claims of the Latter-day Saints and the Book of Mormon.

Key Points:

  • Morrish warns against the deception of the Latter-day Saints.
  • Claims the Book of Mormon is a forgery with wicked designs.
  • Argues LDS teachings are not grounded in the Bible.
  • Book of Mormon claimed to contain the fullness of the gospel.
  • Morrish disputes LDS claims of additional necessary revelation.
  • Contrasts LDS teachings with biblical scripture on salvation.
  • Accuses LDS of teaching doctrines that contradict the Bible.
  • Urges adherence to biblical truth over new revelations.

history.author: 체스터 카운티의 자선가
history.citation: 체스터 카운티의 자선자. 몰몬교의 마스킹은 불충분 한 무단으로 보였고, Bennett의 답변이 답하고 2-24를 답변했습니다. 필라델피아 : T. K. & P. ​​G. Collins, 1840. 몰몬경과 미스터. Bennett의 답변, 답변 및 거부 된 __________________
history.teaser:
A critical examination and refutation of Mormonism and specific replies to claims made by S. Bennett, presenting the sect as deeply flawed and deceptive.

Key Points:

  • Intended to expose errors and blasphemies of Mormonism.
  • Claims Mormons beyond reach of reason or Scripture.
  • Describes Mormons as characterized by slander, imposture, and lying.
  • Attempts to dismantle the authenticity of the Book of Mormon.
  • Compares Mormon revelations unfavorably to biblical revelations.
  • Refutes claims about ancient American civilizations and languages.
  • Questions the veracity and intentions behind Mormon testimonies.
  • Criticizes the perceived dangers of Mormonism to community welfare.

history.author: 프랫, 오슨, 1811-1881
history.citation: Pratt, Orson. 몇 가지 놀라운 비전과 늦은 미국의 늦은 발견의 흥미로운 설명 고대 미국 기록, 3-31. 에딘버러 : Ballantyne와 Hughes, 1840.
history.teaser:
A detailed account by Orson Pratt about the visions Joseph Smith had, the discovery of the ancient American records (Book of Mormon), and the early doctrines of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.

Key Points:

  • Joseph Smith’s early life and first vision of God and Jesus.
  • Angel Moroni’s visitation and direction to ancient records.
  • Translation of the Book of Mormon into English.
  • Opposition and persecution faced by Joseph Smith.
  • Foundational doctrines of repentance, baptism, and receiving the Holy Ghost.
  • Organization of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints in 1830.
  • Belief in continuous revelation and prophecy.
  • Urgent call to repentance in preparation for the Second Coming of Christ.

history.author: 테일러, 존, 1808-1887
history.citation: 테일러, 존. Calumny가 거부되었고 진실은 옹호했습니다. Robert Heys, Wesleyan 장관의 두 번째 웨소리안 장관, 더글라스의 WeSleyan 감리교 사회, 1-12. 리버풀 : J. Tompkins, 1840.
history.teaser:
A detailed rebuttal by John Taylor against accusations made by Rev. Robert Heys concerning the Book of Mormon and Latter-day Saint beliefs.

Key Points:

  • Persecution as evidence of faith’s purity, not its falsehood
  • Defense against claims of malicious and contradictory statements
  • Refutation of the claim that the Book of Mormon is a romantic fiction
  • Comparison of Book of Mormon teachings with Biblical scripture
  • Clarification on doctrines such as repentance, baptism, and salvation
  • Assertion that infant baptism is not supported by scripture
  • Accusation of inconsistency and heresy within Wesleyan Methodism
  • Invitation for a public discussion based on Biblical scripture

history.citation: 요한 로빈슨과 몰몬교에 관한 주인 사이의 조금 이야기, 원산지, 부조리 및 불경사, 1-8. Bedford : W. White, 1840.
history.teaser:
A skeptical dialogue from 1840, debunking Mormonism through a fictional conversation between a master and his servant.

Key Points:

  • The Book of Mormon is claimed to originate from Solomon Spalding’s manuscript.
  • Sidney Rigdon is suspected of copying Spalding’s work for the Book of Mormon.
  • The dialogue criticizes the anachronistic mention of a mariner’s compass in the Book of Mormon.
  • It argues the physical impossibility of the golden plates’ described size and weight.
  • Translation errors in the Book of Mormon are highlighted as proof against its divine origin.
  • The dialogue refutes Mormon claims of a new revelation with scriptural counterarguments.
  • Mormon doctrines are portrayed as absurd, impious, and blasphemous.
  • The narrative aims to dissuade people from joining the Mormon movement.

history.author: 윈체스터, 벤자민
history.citation: 윈체스터, 벤자민. Rev. H. Perkins가 후기 성도에 대한 종교적 의견과 신앙에 대한 H. Perkins와 가장 두려운 오류와 허위 중 일부는 1-12로서 1840.
history.teaser:
A detailed rebuttal by Benjamin Winchester to Rev. H. Perkins’ lecture on the beliefs of the Latter-day Saints, correcting misconceptions and errors.

Key Points:

  • Winchester defends the Latter-day Saints against Perkins’ criticisms.
  • Addresses Perkins’ misuse of scripture to attack Mormon beliefs.
  • Counters Perkins’ claim that Latter-day Saints preach new doctrines.
  • Refutes Perkins’ assertions about the nonexistence of prophets after the apostles.
  • Challenges Perkins’ understanding of the role of miracles in faith.
  • Disagrees with Perkins’ interpretation of the pre-existence of spirits.
  • Defends the necessity of baptism for salvation against Perkins’ views.
  • Criticizes Perkins for spreading falsehoods about the Latter-day Saints.

history.author: 하이닝, 사무엘
history.citation: Haining, Samuel. 몰몬교가 성소의 균형을 유지하고를 원한다 : 4 강의 물질, 1-66. Douglas : Robert Fargher, 1840. 첫 번째 강의 [* 읽을 수 없음 *]
history.teaser:
A detailed critique and rebuttal of the Book of Mormon and the claims of its early followers, emphasizing its deviation from traditional Christian teachings and the Bible.

Key Points:

  • Claims of the Book of Mormon are unfounded and presumptuous.
  • Its teachings deviate significantly from the Bible.
  • Claims of direct revelations and visions are scrutinized.
  • The book is criticized for adding to the Bible.
  • Mormon priesthood claims are considered unscriptural.
  • The physical evidence and witnesses for the book are questioned.
  • Caution is advised against accepting new revelations beyond the Bible.
  • Adherence to the Bible alone is strongly advocated.

history.author: 테일러, 존, 1808-1887
history.document: 진실방어와 방법론은 균형에 무게를 두고 있으며 부족한 것을 발견한다.
history.citation: 테일러, 존. 진리는 균형을 유지하고 감염법이 균형을 이루고 발견 : Robert Heys, Wesleyan의 세 번째 주소에 대한 답장이었습니다. Douglas의 Wesleyan 감리교 사회와 그 주변 (1-12). 리버풀 : J. Tompkins, 1840. Music Hall, Bold Street
history.teaser:
A comprehensive critique of Methodism in comparison to LDS beliefs, focusing on the discrepancies between Methodist practices and what John Taylor identifies as true Christian doctrine according to the Latter-Day Saint movement.

Key Points:

  • John Taylor challenges Methodist doctrines and practices.
  • Methodism accused of deviating from scriptural truths.
  • Contrasts Methodist and LDS views on apostles, prophets, and spiritual gifts.
  • Criticizes Methodist reliance on human authority for ministerial roles.
  • Disputes Methodist teachings on God’s nature and the Trinity.
  • Questions Methodist practices of baptism and church discipline.
  • Asserts LDS superiority in adherence to biblical teachings.
  • Encourages Methodists to remove the “beam out of their own eye”.

history.author: 프랫, 팔리 P. (팔리 파커), 1807-1857
history.citation: Pratt, Parley P. "Mormonites. 새로운 시대의 편집자에게. " 시간과 계절 (상거래, 일리노이 주) 1, 아니오. 3 (1840년 1월):45-46쪽. 파레폴에서 재 인쇄했다. Pratt "Mormonites. 새로운 시대의 편집자에게. " (뉴욕) (1839년 11월 27일).
history.teaser:
Parley P. Pratt defends the Book of Mormon and the Latter-Day Saint movement against accusations and clarifies misconceptions.

Key Points:

  • Pratt addresses an article signed by “Matilda Davidson”.
  • Clarifies there’s no such book as the “Mormon Bible”.
  • LDS believe in the Bible and the Book of Mormon.
  • Refutes accusations of knavery and superstition.
  • Denies Sidney Rigdon’s alleged connection to a printing office.
  • Corrects the founding location and Rigdon’s involvement.
  • Challenges the Spaulding manuscript theory.
  • Requests fairness in the portrayal of the Latter-Day Saint movement.

history.author: 프랫, 팔리 P. (팔리 파커), 1807-1857
history.citation: Pratt, Parley P. "몰몬경에 대한 반대" 후기 성도 밀레니엄 스타 (맨체스터, 잉글랜드) 1, 아니오. 7 (1840년 11월):185-87쪽.
history.teaser:
An article by Parley P. Pratt defending the Book of Mormon against common criticisms of its validity and the possibility of new revelation.

Key Points:

  • Pratt addresses the absurdity of objections against the Book of Mormon.
  • Critics misuse Bible verses to argue against further revelation.
  • Misinterpretation of Paul’s words used to discredit new scriptures.
  • Many New Testament writings occurred after Paul’s declarations.
  • Timothy’s familiarity with scriptures refers to the Old Testament.
  • New Testament necessity parallels that of the Book of Mormon.
  • Revelation 22:18 misunderstood as a closure to divine revelation.
  • Book of Mormon is not an addition to John’s Revelation but a separate revelation.

history.citation: 워싱턴의 시민들과 공공 균열에 대한 교회의 예수 그리스도의 교회의 교회의 교회의 교회의 복음의 판사와 판사와의 PRATT 사역자들의 판사와 판사의 판사와 공개적 인 것 시간과 계절 상거래, 일리노이 주) 1, 아니오. 5 (3 월 1840):69쪽.
history.teaser:
An address by Judge Higbee and Parley P. Pratt defending the Book of Mormon and its significance to Christianity and history.

Key Points:

  • Affirms belief in the Book of Mormon alongside the Bible
  • Book of Mormon seen as a historical and religious record
  • Claims Book of Mormon does not exclude the Bible
  • Indicates that Book of Mormon corroborates biblical scriptures
  • Compares discovery of Book of Mormon to hypothetical discoveries of other ancient records
  • Views the Book of Mormon as revealing ancient American events
  • Predicts the Book of Mormon’s significance will be recognized globally
  • Suggests current opposition to the Book of Mormon is due to ignorance

history.author: 시린, M.
history.citation: Sirrine, M. "형제. 스미스 & 로빈슨. " 시간과 계절 (상거래, 일리노이 주) 1, 아니오. 5 (3 월 1840):73-74쪽.
history.teaser:
A letter describing the spread of the Latter-day Saint movement in Michigan and a public debate on the Book of Mormon’s divine origin.

Key Points:

  • M. Sirrine reports on missionary work in Michigan
  • Organized a church of 11 members in Lenawee County
  • Orson Pratt’s visit and sermons boosted interest
  • Public debate on the Book of Mormon’s divine revelation
  • Debate had a large audience and formal structure
  • Book of Mormon defended successfully in debate
  • Increased demand for the Book of Mormon and hymn books
  • Preaches 5-6 times a week due to high demand

history.author: 솔직함
history.citation: 칸막. Christian Advocate And Journal (뉴욕) (뉴욕) (1840년 3월 6일).
history.teaser:
An article from the Christian Advocate and Journal detailing Joseph Smith’s visit to Washington D.C., his public speaking, and assertions about the Book of Mormon.

Key Points:

  • Joseph Smith in Washington D.C. seeking remuneration for Missouri losses
  • Smith described as inspired to write the Book of Mormon
  • Smith’s appearance and manner noted as prepossessing and shrewd
  • Smith’s teachings compared to Campbelites, emphasizes baptism for remission of sins
  • Smith cautious about discussing the Book of Mormon in detail
  • Smith asserts he solely wrote the Book of Mormon, aligning with the Bible
  • Smith confirms the Book of Mormon was written on gold plates in Egyptian and Chaldee
  • Smith denies Mrs. Davidson’s claim that her husband wrote the Book of Mormon

history.author: 팔머, 아브라함
history.document: 미주리의 모빙 정신 일리노이에서 다시 불붙다
history.citation: 성지 순례자. "일리노이 주에서 미주리 렌트 링의 모방 정신." 일리노이 레지스터 (스프링 필드, 일리노이) (3월 20일).
history.teaser:
A report on the persecution of a Methodist man for owning a Book of Mormon, leading to the book’s burning.

Key Points:

  • Mr. Clark reprimanded for owning the Book of Mormon
  • Deprived of his position as class leader
  • Book demanded by preachers, bought and burned
  • Book’s burning occurred during a Quarterly Conference meeting
  • Preacher Mr. Watt suggested burning Mormons if necessary

history.author: 이런, 조지 W.
history.citation: Gee, George W. "Adams Co. 아프다. 3월 30일, 1840 년. Messrs. 로빈슨과 스미스. " 시간 및 계절 (상거래, 일리노이) 1, 아니오. 6 (1840년 4월):88쪽.
history.teaser:
A letter published in the Times and Seasons detailing George W. Gee’s missionary experiences in Tennessee, his debates on the legitimacy of the Book of Mormon, and the necessity of apostles and spiritual gifts in the church.

Key Points:

  • Gee’s missionary journey began in November, preaching in Tennessee
  • Encountered prejudice due to falsehoods from Missouri persecutors
  • Joined by Elder J. Moses; together baptized two individuals
  • Preached in Jackson co., resulting in ten baptisms and more believers
  • Obtained 21 subscribers for Times and Seasons; faced demand for books
  • Faced misrepresentation and participated in a three-day public debate
  • Debate topics included the Book of Mormon’s divine inspiration and the necessity of spiritual gifts
  • One baptism followed the debate, with more potential converts

history.citation: 몰몬교 종교적 헤럴드 (Richmond, Virginia) (1840년 4월 9일).
history.teaser:
An article from the Religious Herald offering a critical view on the tenets and practices of the early Latter-Day Saint movement and its founder, Joseph Smith.

Key Points:

  • Mormons compared to Reformers or Campbellites
  • Practice immersion for remission of sins
  • Believe in an earthly New Jerusalem in the Western world
  • Adopted communal living like early disciples and Shakers
  • Book of Mormon criticized as a bungling, stupid production
  • System deemed erroneous, carrying falsehood and imposture
  • Mormonism has many devoted adherents and is increasing
  • Joseph Smith described as inspired but criticized for the Book of Mormon

history.author: 프랫, 팔리 P. (팔리 파커), 1807-1857
history.citation: Pratt, Parley P. "미국에서 고대 기록을 발견했습니다." 후기 성도 밀레니엄 스타 (맨체스터, 영국) 1, 아니오. 2 (6 월 1840):30-37쪽.
history.teaser:
A detailed account by Parley P. Pratt about the discovery and significance of the Book of Mormon.

Key Points:

  • Joseph Smith visited by an angel at age 17
  • Angel revealed existence of ancient sacred records
  • Records found in Manchester, New York, on September 22, 1827
  • Records written in Egyptian on gold plates
  • Included Urim and Thummim for translation
  • Records translated into English, published in 1830
  • Describes two ancient American civilizations
  • Christ visited America after his resurrection

history.citation: 서적!!! 시간과 계절 (Nauvoo, 일리노이) 1, 아니오. 9 (7월 1840일):139-40쪽.
history.teaser:
An announcement in the “Times and Seasons” regarding the efforts to meet the high demand for religious books among the Latter-day Saints, including the Book of Mormon.

Key Points:

  • High demand for religious books among the saints
  • Persecution has made it difficult to supply books
  • Book of Mormon being stereotyped and printed in Cincinnati, Ohio
  • Books expected to be available by the first of September
  • Efforts to publish a Hymn Book and a new translation of the scriptures
  • Samuel Bent and Geo. W. Harris appointed as traveling agents for the project
  • Encouragement for saints to subscribe and pay in advance
  • Financial contributions seen as beneficial for the soul

history.author: 프랫, 팔리 P. (팔리 파커), 1807-1857
history.citation: Pratt, Parley P. 흥미로운 발견. " 후기 성도 밀레니엄 별 (맨체스터, 영국) 1, 아니오. 4 (8 월 1840):101-103쪽.
history.teaser:
Parley P. Pratt discusses archaeological discoveries that seem to support the historical claims made in the Book of Mormon.

Key Points:

  • Scandinavian relics found in South America suggest ancient voyages
  • Roman coins discovered in England, buried since around 426 AD
  • General acceptance of archaeological finds contrasted with skepticism towards the Book of Mormon
  • Comparison of preservation of ancient records and artifacts
  • Questioning why discoveries of ancient cities and coins are readily accepted but ancient records like the Book of Mormon are not
  • Parallel between ancient records hidden by divine command and secular discoveries
  • Assertion that both the Book of Mormon and the Bible are true

history.citation: 미국의 유물. " 후기 성도 밀레니엄 별 (맨체스터, 영국) 1, 아니오. 5 (1840년 9월) : 1 18.
history.teaser:
An article from the Latter-day Saints Millennial Star discussing discoveries of ancient American artifacts potentially supporting the Book of Mormon narrative.

Key Points:

  • Stephens and Catherwood made discoveries in Central America
  • Found statues, monuments, and altars with hieroglyphics
  • Some monuments are movable to the United States
  • Discoveries include a giant head and elegantly sculptured altars
  • Monuments similar to those found at Palenque
  • Explorers plan to continue their journey to Palenque and Mexico
  • Findings viewed as supporting evidence for the Book of Mormon

history.author: 클라크, 존 A. (존 알론조), 1801-1843
history.citation: Clark, John A. "그런데 수집. 아뇨. " Episcopal Recorder 필라델피아, 펜실베니아 (Pennsylvania)) (1840년 9월 5일):94쪽.
history.teaser:
An article by John A. Clark discussing the origins and implications of the Mormon faith.

Key Points:

  • Mormonism gaining moral and political importance
  • Organized under a prophet, claiming divine inspiration
  • Mormonism’s rapid spread and extensive missionary efforts
  • Appeals to love of the marvellous and additional revelation
  • Persecution in Missouri strengthened Mormonism
  • Origin story involving Joseph Smith and golden plates
  • Martin Harris’s visit to consult with learned men
  • Implications of a new revelation alongside the Bible

history.author: 클라크, 존 A. (존 알론조), 1801-1843
history.citation: Clark, John A. "그런데 수집. No. VII, "Episcopal Recorder (필라델피아, 펜실베니아) 18, 아니오. 25 (9월 12일 1840).
history.teaser:
An article by John A. Clark discussing the origins and criticisms of Mormonism and the Book of Mormon, emphasizing its perceived implausibility and fraudulent nature.

Key Points:

  • Discusses the influence of the Book of Mormon in converting followers.
  • Asserts Joseph Smith and Martin Harris lacked the intellect for its authorship.
  • Claims the Book of Mormon is claimed to be a divine revelation.
  • Highlights public skepticism and suspicion towards Oliver Cowdery’s role.
  • Includes Isaac Hale’s statement criticizing Joseph Smith’s character and actions.
  • Discusses the mysterious loss of 116 manuscript pages and the response.
  • Mentions Sidney Rigdon’s possible involvement and Spaulding’s manuscript theory.
  • Criticizes the credibility of the Book of Mormon’s witnesses, especially Martin Harris.

history.citation: 몰몬교 Episcopal Recorder (필라델피아, 펜실베니아) 18, 아니오. 26 (9월 19일 19월 19일).
history.teaser:
A notice in the Episcopal Recorder about an upcoming publication regarding the Mormons.

Key Points:

  • Upcoming publication about Mormons in the Episcopal Recorder
  • Gleanings by the Way will conclude its sketch on Mormons

history.citation: 몰몬교 Christian Watchman (보스톤) 21, 아니오. 39 (1840년 9월 25일).
history.teaser:
An article from the Christian Watchman expressing skepticism and criticism towards Mormonism, highlighting its rapid spread and alleged miraculous events.

Key Points:

  • Mormonism finds converts rapidly despite opposition
  • Compares Mormonism’s spread to other controversial movements
  • Mormons claim to heal the sick and cast out devils
  • A preacher reportedly cast out a devil witnessed by two men
  • Documents allegedly prove Joseph Smith’s wickedness
  • Mormonism has been publicly and legally investigated as false
  • The article anticipates proving Mormonism as a “cunningly devised fable”
  • Joseph Smith described as coming from a “shiftless family”

history.author: 클라크, 존 A. (존 알론조), 1801-1843
history.citation: Clark, John A. "그런데 수집. No. VIII. " Episcopal Recorder (필라델피아, 펜실베니아) (1840년 9월 26일):106-07쪽.
history.teaser:
An analysis and critique of the Book of Mormon and its narratives by John A. Clark, highlighting skepticism toward its divine origin and expressing concern about its influence.

Key Points:

  • Clark provides an analysis of the Book of Mormon’s content.
  • Observes varying literary quality suggesting multiple authors.
  • Details the narrative of Nephi and his family’s journey.
  • Describes the acquisition of the brass plates from Laban.
  • Nephi’s vision and interpretations align with Christian theology.
  • Critiques the Book of Mormon’s claim of divine authority.
  • Predicts the eventual conversion of Native Americans through Mormonism.
  • Expresses concern about the book’s potential to deceive.

history.author: 클라크, 존 A. (존 알론조), 1801-1843
history.citation: Clark, John A. "그런데 수집. 아뇨. IX. " Episcopal Recorder (필라델피아, 펜실베니아) (10월 1840일 3월 3일):110-11쪽.
history.teaser:
An Episcopal clergyman’s critique and summary of the Book of Mormon and its narratives, highlighting its origins and key events.

Key Points:

  • Mormon is named after a significant character and location in the narrative.
  • Mormon compiled the sacred canon contained in the Book of Mormon.
  • The narrative includes prophets, migrations, and divine interventions.
  • Alma and his preaching at the waters of Mormon are pivotal.
  • The story includes accounts of conversion, baptism, and establishment of churches.
  • Describes the translation of ancient records by Mosiah, using interpreters.
  • Mentions significant prophecies and signs related to Christ’s life and death.
  • Concludes with the downfall of the Nephites and the preservation of their records by Moroni.

history.author: 클라크, 존 A. (존 알론조), 1801-1843
history.citation: Clark, John A. "No. x를 방해합니다." Episcopal Recorder (필라델피아, 펜실베니아) (10월 1840일 10월 10일):114-15쪽.
history.teaser:
A critical account by John A. Clark detailing his observations and thoughts on the Mormon faith and its spread.

Key Points:

  • Clark is surprised by the rapid spread of Mormonism.
  • Mormonism’s success in converting members from orthodox churches.
  • No believers in Mormonism’s birthplace, suggesting skepticism from those familiar with its origins.
  • Martin Harris, a key witness for Mormonism, made unfulfilled prophecies.
  • Mormons engaged in a failed banking venture, causing rifts among leaders.
  • Mormons in the area keep peculiar beliefs private, focusing on common Christian topics.
  • Mormons attempting to rebrand as “Latter-day Saints” and downplay unique doctrines.
  • Joseph Young’s statement in Boston avoids mentioning core Mormon beliefs.

history.citation: 남자의 섬에 대한 공개 토론. 후기 성도 밀레니엄 별 (맨체스터, 영국) 1, 아니오. 7 (1840년 11월):178-80쪽. "Isleof 남자에 대한 공개 토론"에서 다시 인쇄했습니다. Manx 자유주의 (아일 맨) (10월 4일).
history.teaser:
A detailed account of a public debate between a Latter-Day Saint missionary and a critic on the Isle of Man, highlighting the challenges faced when presenting and defending new religious ideas.

Key Points:

  • LDS missionary Mr. Taylor was challenged by critics during a lecture.
  • A public debate was arranged to discuss the criticisms.

  • Scott highlights perceived inconsistencies in prophecies.
  • Figurative language often found in prophecy is noted.
  • Book of Mormon described as lacking symbolic depth.
  • Lehi’s prophecies are criticized as simplistic and derivative.
  • Comparison of Lehi’s and Nephi’s visions to New Testament.
  • Claims Book of Mormon mixes New Testament with modern divinity.
  • Scott accuses Joseph Smith of plain speaking but dishonesty.
  • Concludes with a strong critique of the Book of Mormon’s profanity.

history.citation: 상위 미시시피스에서. 서쪽에 대한 편지. 세 번째. Nauvoo-Mormon 종교. 시간과 계절 (Nauvoo, 일리노이 주) 2, 아니오. 8 (2월 15일 1541):322-24쪽.
history.teaser:
A detailed account of Nauvoo, Illinois, and the religious beliefs of the Mormons as observed and reported by a visitor to the city.

Key Points:

  • Nauvoo, formerly Commerce, is now a rapidly growing Mormon settlement.
  • About 3000 inhabitants and 300 buildings have been added.
  • Joseph Smith described as a muscular, coarse-looking man, a natural leader.
  • Mormons view the Book of Mormon as an additional revelation.
  • It is believed to detail the history of the house of Ephraim.
  • Joseph Smith received divine guidance to translate brass plates.
  • Mormons seen as generally conscientious and more pitied than despised.
  • Editor notes that the article needs corrections regarding Mormon faith.

history.author: 윈체스터, 벤자민, 1817-1901
history.citation: 윈체스터, 벤자민. "계시록의 지속적인 목적"복음 반사경 (필라델피아) 1, 아니오. 4 (2월 15일 1511):89-96쪽.
history.teaser:
An analysis by Benjamin Winchester on the necessity and purpose of continuous revelation within the Latter-Day Saint movement, arguing against the idea that new revelations imply a new gospel.

Key Points:

  • Continuous revelation is a distinctive feature of the Latter-Day Saints.
  • New revelations do not introduce a new gospel.
  • Revelations often provide guidance for temporal safety and specific tasks.
  • Historical examples of revelation directing actions of biblical figures.
  • Every dispensation or epoch required adapted revelations for its tasks.
  • The Gospel and its principles remain constant across ages.
  • The Latter-Day Saints do not preach a new gospel, but continue in the original.
  • Winchester criticizes the misunderstanding of continuous revelation by other Christian denominations.

history.author: 디스시풀러스(및 Parley P. Pratt)
history.citation: Dispipulus [및 Parley P. Pratt]. "별 편집자에게." 후기 성도 밀레니엄 스타 (맨체스터, 영국) 1, 아니오. 11 (3 월 18411):281쪽.
history.teaser:
A letter to the editor of the Latter-day Saints Millennial Star seeking clarification on the beliefs and practices of the LDS Church, with answers provided to the inquiries.

Key Points:

  • Book of Mormon has multiple witnesses beyond Joseph Smith
  • Conditions for church membership include faith, repentance, baptism by immersion
  • Christ’s appearance in America was ancient, not recent
  • Apostles and officers commissioned by revelations, not by Christ’s personal appearance
  • All members can possess miraculous gifts proportional to their faith

history.author: 테일러, 존, 1808-1887
history.citation: 테일러, 존. "별 편집자에게." 후기 성도 밀레니엄 별 (맨체스터, 영국) 1, 아니오. 11 (3 월 18411):276-80쪽.
history.teaser:
John Taylor’s letter to the editor detailing his experiences and debates in Liverpool and Isle of Man, defending the Latter-Day Saint movement against critics.

Key Points:

  • Taylor responds to criticisms of Mormonism in public lectures
  • Faced opposition from Methodist and Primitive Methodist preachers
  • Public debates helped dispel misconceptions about LDS teachings
  • Encounters with a Methodist preacher who self-appointed his mission
  • Discusses the challenge of defending LDS principles against biased critics
  • Highlights successful public defense against attacks on Mormon doctrines
  • Describes growth of LDS church in Isle of Man and Liverpool
  • Mentions baptisms as evidence of the truth prevailing

history.author: 스콧, 월터
history.citation: Scott, Walter. "몰몬경 성경 - 아니. III. " 전도자 (카르타고, 오하이오) 9, 아니오. 3 (3월 1일 1841년 3월 1일):62-65쪽.
history.teaser:
A critical examination of the Book of Mormon’s claims and its comparison to biblical prophecies.

Key Points:

  • Scott critiques a Mormon preacher’s interpretation of Ezekiel.
  • The preacher claims the Book of Mormon was predicted by Jewish prophets.
  • Scott dismisses the interpretation as lacking sense and relevance.
  • Claims of ancient Christianity in the Americas are examined.
  • The Book of Mormon’s account of baptism is scrutinized.
  • Scott argues the Book of Mormon cannot convincingly predate Christianity.
  • The legitimacy and originality of the Book of Mormon are questioned.
  • Scott concludes the Book of Mormon is a misguided fabrication.

history.author: 윈체스터, 벤자민, 1817-1901
history.citation: 윈체스터, 벤자민. "계시록의 대상." 복음 반사경 (필라델피아) 1, 아니오. 5 (1841년 3월 1일):97-120쪽.
history.teaser:
A detailed analysis of Benjamin Winchester’s exposition on the importance of continuous revelation in the early Latter-Day Saint movement, focusing on the integration of the Book of Mormon into the religious narrative.

Key Points:

  • Winchester emphasizes the necessity of ongoing revelation.
  • Argues against the notion that revelation ended with the apostles.
  • Discusses the Book of Mormon as a form of modern revelation.
  • Highlights opposition and skepticism towards new revelations.
  • Draws parallels between ancient and modern prophets.
  • Mentions prophecies indicating the emergence of new scriptures.
  • Asserts the Book of Mormon fulfills biblical prophecies.
  • Views the Book of Mormon as crucial for understanding God’s will in contemporary times.

history.citation: 시간과 계절 (Nauvoo, 일리노이) 2, 아니오. 10 (3월 15일 15 일):4쪽.
history.teaser:
An article from the “Times and Seasons” defending the authenticity and divine origin of the Book of Mormon against misconceptions and criticisms.

Key Points:

  • Clarifies that Mormon was a prophet who lived 400 years after Christ
  • The Book of Mormon considered an additional revelation
  • Book of Mormon provides history of ancient people on American continent
  • Revelation of Book of Mormon plates to Joseph Smith by an angel
  • Discussion on the credibility of angelic visitations in modern times
  • Arguments against the cessation of revelation and divine visitations
  • Claims of consistent divine guidance across eras
  • Endorsement of the Book of Mormon’s authenticity through witnesses

history.author: 밴스, 윌리엄 R.
history.citation: Vance, William R. "Messrs. Smith & Robinson, Pekin, Tenn. 제 3 회 Ferbuary 1841. " 시간과 계절 (Nauvoo, 일리노이) 2, 아니오. 10 (3월 15일 1841년 3월 15일):349-50쪽.
history.teaser:
A letter to the editors of Times and Seasons expressing surprise and admiration upon discovering the content and purpose of the Book of Mormon and LDS Church publications.

Key Points:

  • William R. Vance writes about his discovery of LDS texts
  • He is surprised the Book of Mormon is not a replacement for the Bible
  • Vance finds the Book of Mormon corroborates the Bible
  • The Doctrine and Covenants contains church regulation principles
  • The Voice of Warning is praised for its truth and reason
  • Vance is astonished by the persecution of Latter Day Saints
  • He criticizes violence in the name of religion
  • Divine Providence led him to these texts, preventing his fall into infidelity

history.author: 윈체스터, 벤자민, 1817-1901
history.citation: 윈체스터, 벤자민. "몰몬경의 주장이 확립 된 - 알소드 펜드." 복음 반사기 (필라델피아) 1, 아니오. 6 (3월 15일 1841년 3월 15일):121-28쪽.
history.teaser:
An article by Benjamin Winchester in The Gospel Reflector defending the Book of Mormon and outlining its significance and the fulfillment of its prophecies.

Key Points:

  • The Book of Mormon is meant to increase joy and understanding among the meek and poor.
  • It is intended to bring those who have erred in spirit to understanding.
  • The Book of Mormon reveals important previously unknown history and the origin of the American Indians.
  • It contains prophecies concerning this generation and provides clarity on doctrines.
  • The Book of Mormon is seen as a tool to gather Israel and prepare for the Millennium.
  • It is associated with the tribe of Ephraim in gathering the people of God.
  • The Book of Mormon is defended as a genuine record, translated by the power of God.
  • Witness testimonies affirm its truthfulness, emphasizing belief until proven otherwise by revelation.

history.citation: 침례교와 후기 성도의 차이점. 노스 스태포드 셔 메레리에서. 후기 성도 밀레니엄 별 (맨체스터, 영국) 1, 아니오. 12 (1841년 4월):296-99쪽.
history.teaser:
An article contrasting the beliefs and practices of Baptists with those of Latter-Day Saints, emphasizing significant doctrinal differences.

Key Points:

  • Baptists require evidence of repentance before baptism; Saints do not
  • Saints practice laying on of hands post-baptism; Baptists disdain it
  • Saints claim extraordinary gifts and power of healing; Baptists reject these
  • Saints accept additional scripture beyond the Bible; Baptists adhere strictly to the Bible
  • Saints have two priesthoods with claims of spiritual authority; Baptists do not recognize these
  • Saints’ practices contrasted with early Christian (Former-day Saints) practices
  • Article defends Baptists’ doctrinal purity against perceived LDS distortions
  • Highlights fundamental doctrinal differences between the two faiths

history.author: 윈체스터, 벤자민, 1817-1901
history.citation: 윈체스터, 벤자민. "시온의 위치 또는 새로운 예루살렘." 복음 반사경 (필라델피아) 1, 아니오. 8 (4월 15일 1841년 4월 15일):213-17쪽.
history.teaser:
An exploration by Benjamin Winchester on the distinct locations and purposes of the biblical Zion in Jerusalem and the prophesied New Jerusalem or Zion in the Americas, in the context of Latter-day Saint beliefs.

Key Points:

  • Zion for the Millennium distinct from Zion at Jerusalem
  • Zion at Jerusalem founded by Melchizedek, called Salem
  • Prophecy points to a New Jerusalem in America
  • David and Isaiah suggest Zion’s location on the North American continent
  • Book of Mormon asserts New Jerusalem on American land
  • America is a promised land to the tribe of Joseph
  • Zion and Jerusalem as two central places of gathering
  • Eventual unification of continents prophesied, fulfilling “thy land shall be married”

history.citation: 몰몬교, 또는 익히는 것이 노출되었습니다. 웨스턴 레코더 (Zanesville, Ohio) (1841년 4월 28일).
history.teaser:
An advertisement for a pamphlet exposing Mormonism as a scheme and fraud, detailing its origins and the actions of its leaders.

Key Points:

  • Pamphlet exposes the discovery and translation of the golden plates
  • Details on the Kirtland temple, bank, and spread of Mormonism
  • Claims two hundred thousand dollars in fake bank notes circulated
  • Describes efforts to rid Frankford, Pa., of Mormons
  • Highlights the “depraved and swindling character” of Mormon leaders
  • Cites evidence from documents printed by the US Senate
  • Compares Mormon leaders to the notorious swindler Mathias
  • Intended as a caution against Mormonism’s “wicked devices”

history.author: 프랫, 팔리 P. (팔리 파커) 1807-1857
history.citation: Pratt, Parley P. "Athenīum에게 답장 : 진실을 반대하는 무지와 폴리의 박람회가됩니다." 후기 성도의 밀레니엄 스타 (맨체스터, 영국) 2, 아니오. 1 (5 월 1841):1-5쪽.
history.teaser:
Parley P. Pratt’s defense of the Book of Mormon and early Latter-day Saint beliefs against criticisms published in the Athenæum.

Key Points:

  • Pratt responds to criticisms and comparisons to Islam and Matthias.
  • Defends the Book of Mormon’s mention of advanced technology like the compass.
  • Challenges the criticism of using “Greek” terms like Christ and Alpha-Omega.
  • Argues against the claim of a hidden Book of Doctrine and Covenants.
  • Addresses accusations of forgery and the Spaulding theory.
  • Refutes claims of commanded communal living in the Book of Mormon.
  • Discusses persecution and legal troubles in Missouri.
  • Clarifies misconceptions about Nauvoo’s Hebrew origin and financial matters.

history.author: 스콧, 월터
history.citation: Scott, Walter. "몰몬경 성경 - 아니. IV. " 전도자 (카르타고, 오하이오) 9, 아니오. 5 (5월 1일 1841):111-15쪽.
history.teaser:
An article by Walter Scott critiquing the Book of Mormon and Mormon practices, including their construction of temples and the priesthood.

Key Points:

  • Scott critiques the Mormon response to criticism.
  • He argues the Book of Mormon confutes itself.
  • Mentions the construction of temples by Mormons as influenced by the Book of Mormon.
  • Discusses the Mormon community’s growth and their gaining of exclusive privileges.
  • Criticizes the Mormon’s violent history and potential future conflicts.
  • Compares Mormon priesthood to biblical priesthood inaccurately.
  • Notes the absurdity of a Melchisedeckian priesthood pre-Christ in America.
  • Concludes by mentioning three books written against Mormonism.

history.citation: 몰몬교 (스코틀랜드 사람에서). 기독교 개혁자; 또는 단위 아나리아 잡지 및 검토 8 (6 월 1841):386쪽.
history.teaser:
A critical article from “The Christian Reformer” discussing the activities of Mormon missionaries in Edinburgh and the origins of the Book of Mormon.

Key Points:

  • Mormon missionaries labeled as impostors in Edinburgh
  • Claims of angelic interaction and miraculous powers
  • Book of Mormon said to be authored by Solomon Spaulding
  • Spaulding’s manuscript allegedly copied by Sidney Rigdon
  • Fraud exposed by Spaulding’s family and published declarations
  • J. B. Rollo, a former elder, exposed Mormonism as a scam
  • Orson Pratt accused of financial exploitation in the name of faith
  • Mormonism’s followers described as “doltish and illiterate”

history.author: 스콧, 월터
history.citation: Scott, Walter. "몰몬경 성경 - 아니. V." 전도자 (카르타고, 오하이오) 9, 아니오. 6 (1841년 6월 1일):132-36쪽.
history.teaser:
A critical account by Walter Scott regarding the early activities and practices of the Mormon community, including Sidney Rigdon’s role.

Key Points:

  • Document written by Josiah Jones, critical of Mormons
  • Describes early Mormon preaching and baptism practices
  • Claims Sidney Rigdon was re-baptized and influenced by Mormons
  • Describes visions, prophecies, and miraculous claims among Mormons
  • Young members experienced visions and spiritual manifestations
  • Some members claimed to prophesy and perform miracles
  • Walter Scott argues Mormonism adopted baptism practices from Rigdon
  • Scott criticizes Mormonism as an imposture and deviation from true gospel

history.document: 미국 유물~몰몬의 책에 대한 더 많은 증거
history.citation: 미국 고함 - 몰몬경의 증거가 많습니다. 시간과 계절 (Nauvoo, 일리노이 주) 2, 아니오. 16 (6월 15일 1841년 6월 15일):440-42쪽.
history.teaser:
An article from “Times and Seasons” discussing the findings of travelers in Central America as evidence supporting the Book of Mormon.

Key Points:

  • Discovery of ancient Central American ruins supports Book of Mormon
  • Travelers found massive stone structures and sophisticated art
  • Ruins suggest a highly skilled, ancient civilization once existed
  • Evidence includes statues, pyramids, and hieroglyphics
  • Findings similar to ancient Egyptian and other civilizations’ artifacts
  • Some ruins believed to have religious or ceremonial significance
  • Travelers visited eight ruined cities, emphasizing the civilization’s extent
  • Discoveries fuel debate on historical accuracy of the Book of Mormon

history.citation: Martin Harris, 몰몬경 로체스터 일일 민주당 (뉴욕) (1841년 6월 23일).
history.teaser:
An 1841 newspaper article discussing the rumored death of Martin Harris, an early supporter of the Book of Mormon, and reflecting on his life and contributions to the Mormon movement.

Key Points:

  • Rumored murder of Martin Harris near Nauvoo
  • Regarded as honest but deluded by neighbors
  • Early and wealthy supporter of Mormonism
  • Funded Mormonism’s early stages, including printing of the Book of Mormon
  • Mortgaged farm for Book of Mormon publication, ultimately losing it
  • Remained firm in Mormonism belief despite financial losses
  • Shifted from supporter to critic of Mormonism before rumored death
  • Call for investigation into Harris’s rumored murder

history.citation: Painesville Telegraph (오하이오) (1841년 6월 30일).
history.teaser:
An erroneous report of Martin Harris’s death circulated, which the Painesville Telegraph corrects, also discussing Harris’s views on Mormonism.

Key Points:

  • Martin Harris was falsely reported dead
  • Harris had been lecturing against the Mormons in Illinois
  • Rochester Democrat eulogized Harris for his honesty
  • Harris was alive and well in Kirtland at the time of report
  • Harris believes the early work of the LDS Church was divine
  • Harris thinks Joseph Smith became a knave and impostor
  • Harris anticipates a revival of the work through other means

history.citation: 몰몬경과 몰몬생의 책. Athenaeum, 외국 문학 박물관, 과학 및 예술 42 (7월 1841일):370-74쪽.
history.teaser:
An 1841 article from the Athenaeum critically analyzing the origins and content of the Book of Mormon, comparing its reception and propagation to that of a literary forgery.

Key Points:

  • Compares Book of Mormon’s spread to a satire of intellectual progress
  • Discusses Joseph Smith’s claim of divine revelations and visions
  • Compares Smith’s revelations to those claimed by Mohammed
  • Scrutinizes the historical inaccuracies and anachronisms within the text
  • Traces the origin of the Book of Mormon to a manuscript by Solomon Spaulding
  • Mentions the book’s rapid progress in England and its diverse converts
  • Discusses connections between the Mormonites and other religious movements
  • Criticizes the quality and inspiration claims of Mormonite hymns

history.author: 애덤스, 조지 J.
history.citation: Adams, George J. "Sectarian Polly And Wickedness가 나타났습니다. Northampton, 6월 22일, 1841년 6월 22일. " 후기 성도의 밀레니엄 스타 (맨체스터, 영국) 2, 아니오. 3 (7월 1841일):33-37쪽.
history.teaser:
An account by George J. Adams of his missionary efforts and confrontations with sectarian opposition in England.

Key Points:

  • George J. Adams reports on his missionary travels and successes
  • Describes opposition from sectarian priests in Bedford
  • Public debates with sectarians, including newspaper slanders
  • Describes a chaotic public meeting disrupted by opponents
  • Conflicts involve accusations against the LDS Church
  • Adams defends the church using scripture and doctrine
  • Adams and Elder O. Hyde address charges against the Saints
  • Describes growth and expansion of preaching locations

history.document: 미스터 J. B. 롤로의 몰몬교 노출에 대해 응답하라.
history.citation: J. J. B. B. Rollo’s’Mormonism에 답장하십시오. 3 (7 월 18411):43-48쪽. Pratt, Parley P. Preston Chronicle에 답장하십시오."" 후기 성도의 밀레니엄 스타 (맨체스터, 영국) 2, 아니오. 3 (7월 1841일):42-43쪽.
history.teaser:
A detailed rebuttal to J. B. Rollo’s criticisms of Mormonism, defending the doctrines and practices of the Latter-Day Saints.

Key Points:

  • Rejection of accusations of borrowing principles from another society.
  • Clarification that all laws given to Latter-Day Saints are from Christ.
  • Explanation of the Latter-Day Saints’ belief in an earthly inheritance.
  • Defends the practice of purchasing land as consistent with biblical precedent.
  • Addresses accusations of excluding the poor from inheritance.
  • Refutes claims of lacking spiritual gifts and apostolic signs.
  • Corrects misrepresentations about the Book of Mormon and Doctrine and Covenants.
  • Counters critiques of Joseph Smith’s leadership and titles.

history.author: 프랫, Parsey P. (Parley Parker), 1807-1857
history.citation: 몰몬교의 대화. 나 아니라. 시간과 계절 (Nauvoo, 일리노이 주) 2, 아니오. 17 (1841년 7월 1일):456-57쪽.
history.teaser:
Parley P. Pratt’s response to criticisms of Mormonism published in the Preston Chronicle, defending the faith and its prophecies regarding the Native Americans and the future of America.

Key Points:

  • Pratt defends Mormonism against accusations of violence and imperialism.
  • Accusations are compared to historical persecution of Jesus and early Christians.
  • Claims the Book of Mormon prophesies the redemption of the Native Americans.
  • Pratt argues critics are afraid of Mormonism’s success and divine justice.
  • He sees no issue with calling the Gentiles to repentance as per the Book of Mormon.
  • Pratt denies intentions of violence, stating Mormons only act in defense.
  • Asserts Mormonism will defend American liberties if threatened again.
  • Condemns the actions of Missouri officials and their treatment of Mormons.

history.citation: 미국 인디언 또는 레이맨인의 현재 상태와 전망. " 후기 일 성도 ‘천년기 별 (맨체스터, 잉글랜드) 2, 아니오. 3 (7월 2일 1841):40-42쪽.
history.teaser:
A fictional dialogue published in the Times and Seasons that seeks to address and correct misconceptions about Mormonism.

Key Points:

  • Mr. R. dismisses Mormon preaching without listening
  • Mr. M. advocates hearing both sides before judging
  • Mr. M. challenges the basis of rumors and slander against Mormons
  • Discussion of Mormon beliefs and their compatibility with the Bible
  • Mr. M. describes a positive experience with a Mormon preacher
  • Mr. M. invites Mr. R. to listen and converse with a Mormon preacher
  • Mr. R. expresses skepticism but is open to discussion
  • Dialogue highlights importance of direct engagement over hearsay

history.citation: 몰몬경에 대한 대화가 없다. 시간과 계절 (Nauvoo, 일리노이 주) 2, 아니오. 18 (1841년 7월 15일):472-74쪽.
history.teaser:
An article from the Latter-day Saints’ Millennial Star discussing the historical context and future prospects of American Indians, identified as Lamanites, in relation to LDS beliefs and prophecies.

Key Points:

  • American Indians identified as a remnant of Israel, tribe of Joseph
  • Driven and afflicted by Gentiles for the last 300 years
  • United States government allocated land for Indian tribes
  • Gathering of tribes since publication of ancient records in 1830
  • Substantial support provided by the United States to relocated tribes
  • Tribes transitioning from hunting to agriculture and arts
  • Some tribes have become Latter-Day Saints
  • Prediction of a consolidated national identity under US care

history.citation: 번역. 바르샤바 신호 (바르샤바, 일리노이) 2, 아니오. 2 (7월 21일 1841년 7월 21일).
history.teaser:
A discussion on the Book of Mormon, its origin, and its teachings between Mr. Mathews, Mr. Roberts, and Elder Pierce, published in the “Times and Seasons.”

Key Points:

  • Book of Mormon is not a replacement for the Bible
  • Describes the journey of Lehi’s family to the American continent
  • Indians considered descendants of Jews
  • Divisions among Lehi’s descendants led to emergence of Lamanites
  • Christ visited the American continent post-resurrection
  • Discusses the decline and fall of Nephite civilization
  • Modern Indians are seen as degenerate descendants of noble ancestors
  • Book of Mormon seen as shedding light on ancient American civilizations

history.citation: ‘후기의 성도의 성도의 특별 부과 - 모든 좋은 시민들의 중요한 사실을 고려해야한다. 토요일 택배에서. Western Recorder (Zanesville, Ohio) (Zanesville, Ohio) (1841년 7월 21일).

A satirical article from the Warsaw Signal mocking the use of “Reformed Egyptian” names by leaders of the Mormon community in Nauvoo, Illinois.

  • Article mocks Mormon leaders for adopting “Reformed Egyptian” names
  • Claims names like Gazelom and Pilagoram have negative meanings
  • Gazelom supposedly translates to “Presiding Great Devil”
  • Pilagoram allegedly means “Superior Ugly Devil”
  • Nauvoo is interpreted as a dwelling place for devils
  • Article questions the appropriateness of these names for leaders
  • Satirizes the blending of Hebrew and Egyptian languages
  • Mocks the legitimacy of “Reformed Egyptian” as a language

history.citation: 도전. 바르샤바 신호 (바르샤바, 일리노이) 2, 아니오. 2 (7월 21일 1841년 7월 21일).
history.teaser:
An article from the Western Recorder criticizing the practices and beliefs of the early Latter Day Saints (Mormons), highlighting perceived fraud and deception.

Key Points:

  • Claims Mormonism is a swindle and its followers are either knaves or dupes
  • Joseph Smith accused of creating a fraudulent religious movement for personal gain
  • Itinerant Mormon followers accused of begging, stealing, and robbery under religious pretense
  • Smith and other leaders accused of exploiting followers for financial gain
  • Mormon leaders criticized for their pursuit of wealth through deceit

  • Claims of fraudulent banking practices by Mormons to pay debts
  • Criticism of Mormon leaders for issuing worthless paper money

A public challenge issued to Joseph Smith to translate the golden plates in Carthage, Illinois, questioning the authenticity of the Book of Mormon.

  • Promise of a local translator for the reformed Egyptian language
  • Translation to occur before a large congregation
  • Refusal to accept challenge seen as evidence of fraud

A letter published in the Christian Advocate and Journal criticizing Mormonism and detailing its perceived origins and practices.

  • Claims exposure of Mormonism would prevent conversions.
  • Mentions natural superstition as a factor in Mormonism’s spread.

  • Condemns Mormon practices and denunciation of other Christian denominations.

A critical letter published in the Christian Advocate and Journal discussing the origins and content of the Book of Mormon, highlighting perceived absurdities and contradictions.

An 1841 letter to the editor of the Warsaw Signal criticizing the Book of Mormon and its claimed divine origin, using humor and sarcasm.

history.author: 머독, 제임스

An article by James Murdock summarizing an interview with a Mormon minister about the origins and beliefs of the Latter Day Saint movement.

A letter in the Times and Seasons reflecting on the growth and trials of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.

A letter to the editors of the Times & Seasons detailing the missionary efforts and successes in New Rochelle, New York, and discussing the authenticity of the Book of Mormon.

  • Discussion of opposition from local clergy

An article from the Christian Register and Boston Observer detailing a British family’s disillusionment with Mormonism after emigrating to the United States.

An address aimed at clarifying misconceptions and defending the practices and beliefs of the Latter Day Saint movement.

  • Intended to uphold Christian principles and encourage open-mindedness
  • Emphasizes liberty of conscience and respectful religious expression
  • Rejects the use of slander and persecution in religious debate
  • Calls for scriptural investigation of religious matters

  • Discusses a global revolution, more significant than any before.

  • Introduces the Book of Mormon as a key to understanding these events.
