  • The mistreatment of Native Americans and call for justice

history.author: 미스터, R.T.
history.citation: Levi O. C. Nicklin에서 Walter Scott, Pittsburgh, Pittsburgh, Mormonism Inpittsburgh. " 전도자 (카르타고, 오하이오) 10, 아니오. 2 (2월 1일 1842):32-34쪽.
history.teaser:
An 1842 critique of Mormon beliefs and practices, raising concerns about their growing influence and political power.

Key Points:

  • Mormons have twelve stakes for building temples
  • Joseph Smith considered a prophet on par with Isaiah
  • Claims of exclusive truthfulness of the Mormon church
  • Baptism by immersion by an authorized person is mandatory
  • Direct revelation needed to preach or administer ordinances
  • Zion or New Jerusalem is located in Missouri
  • Indians considered lost tribes of Israel to be gathered
  • Joseph Smith’s translation of the Bible includes significant alterations

history.author: 니클린, 레비 O.C.
history.citation: 중앙 아메리카의 폐허후기 성도의 성도의 천년 별 (맨체스터, 영국) 2, 아니오. 11 (3 월 18422):161-65쪽.
history.teaser:
A letter describing a public challenge between a Mormon apostle, John E. Page, and a local religious figure, brother Church, over the authenticity of the Book of Mormon.

Key Points:

  • Public interest was high for a Mormon preaching in Pittsburgh
  • John E. Page, a Mormon apostle, claimed Book of Mormon’s divinity
  • Page referenced discoveries in South America as evidence
  • Clergy initially avoided confrontation, believing Mormonism’s flaws would be self-evident
  • Brother Church accepted the challenge to discuss the Book of Mormon
  • Page shifted discussion to other topics; Church focused on Book of Mormon
  • Page struggled under scrutiny during the public debate
  • Local religious activities continue to thrive, with new baptisms reported

history.citation: 스미스, 요셉. "교회 역사" 시간과 계절 (Nauvoo, 일리노이 주) 3, 아니오. 9 (1842년 3월 1일):706-10쪽.
history.teaser:
An article linking the ruins discovered in Central America by Mr. Stephens to the ancient Nephites described in the Book of Mormon.

Key Points:

  • Mr. Stephens’ explorations reveal remarkable ancient edifices in Central America.
  • Stephens concludes these cities were built by races present during the Spanish invasion.
  • Ruins suggest a highly advanced, indigenous civilization.
  • The article suggests the ruins are of Nephite cities mentioned in the Book of Mormon.
  • Link between modern discovery and ancient records claimed to be revealed by God.
  • The Book of Mormon provides history of a civilization unknown to the rest of the world.
  • Names of Nephite cities and leaders are claimed to match those found by Stephens.
  • The article asserts the Book of Mormon explains the “mystery” of these ancient ruins.

history.author: 스미스, 조셉, 1805-1844
history.citation: 몰몬교의 역사 남부 분기 별 검토 (뉴 올리언즈) 1, 아니오. 2 (1842년 4월):398-413쪽.
history.teaser:
An account by Joseph Smith detailing the origins and beliefs of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, written for a non-member audience.

Key Points:

  • Written at the request of John Wentworth for a history project
  • Smith’s early life and the initial revelation in a grove
  • The visitation by an angel revealing the Book of Mormon
  • The translation of the Book of Mormon through Urim and Thummim
  • Persecutions faced by the early church and migrations
  • Foundation of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
  • Expulsion from Missouri under Governor Boggs’ extermination order
  • Establishment in Nauvoo, Illinois, and the growth of the church

history.citation: 조셉 스미스의 역사 시간과 계절 (Nauvoo, 일리노이 주) 3, 아니오. 12 (1842년 4월 15일):753-54쪽.
history.teaser:
An early critical examination and denunciation of Mormonism and its founder, Joseph Smith, from a secular perspective.

Key Points:

  • Describes Mormonism as a form of mass delusion and imposture.
  • Joseph Smith criticized as a cunning and ambitious impostor.
  • Mormonism’s rapid growth and establishment of communities noted.
  • Mormon missionaries’ success in England highlighted.
  • Discusses the dangers of credulity and lack of critical thinking.
  • Compares Mormonism’s absurdities to historical superstitions and myths.
  • Expresses concern over the sophisticated use of press by Mormons.
  • Critiques the shallow nature of what is often termed “education”.

history.citation: 몰몬교 서양식 기독교 옹호 (신시내티, 오하이오) 9, 아니오. 1 (1842년 4월 22일).
history.teaser:
An account of Joseph Smith’s vision of the angel Nephi, detailing the calling and revelations pertaining to the translation of the Book of Mormon.

Key Points:

  • Joseph Smith describes a vision of a messenger from God
  • Messenger identified as Nephi, later corrected to Moroni
  • Revelation of a book written on gold plates
  • Introduction to the Urim and Thummim for translation
  • Quotes prophecies and scriptures about the coming events
  • Commanded not to show the plates except to those commanded
  • Receives a vision of where the plates were deposited
  • Warned about Satan’s temptation and the importance of purity of intent

history.citation: 몰몬성과 짧고 쉬운 방법. 반 사회주의 자 - 구이 (체스터) 아니오. 8 (5월 1일 1842):142쪽.
history.teaser:
A letter published in the Western Christian Advocate detailing Charles Anthon’s encounter with early Mormonism and his skepticism towards it.

Key Points:

  • Anthon denies being a proselyte to Mormonism
  • Anthon considered the characters shown to him a hoax
  • A countryman presented a transcript of characters for examination
  • The characters were a mix of various alphabetic symbols
  • A story of golden plates and spectacles with translation abilities
  • Anthon advised against selling property for publishing the book
  • Anthon refused to accept a copy of the “golden bible”
  • Anthon suspects the countryman was Joseph Smith himself

history.document: 몰몬교도들과 함께 하는 짧고 쉬운 방법
history.citation: 켄터키에서 발견 된 미라의 카타콤. 시간과 계절 (Nauvoo, 일리노이 주) 3, 아니오. 13 (5월 1842일):781-82쪽.
history.teaser:
An 1842 critique in the Anti-Socialist Gazette of the Book of Mormon, accusing it of being a blasphemous parody of the Bible.

Key Points:

  • Accuses the Book of Mormon of copying the Bible’s translation word for word
  • Describes the Book of Mormon as a blasphemous parody
  • Points out that it includes even minor errors found in the Bible
  • Asserts that claimed divine origin of Book of Mormon is exposed as a deception
  • Recommends pressing the issue of identical translations to confound believers
  • Highlights the absurdity of the narrative found in the Book of Mormon
  • Compares the Book of Mormon’s account unfavorably to the Bible’s sublimity
  • Specifically criticizes the narrative of barges built by the brother of Jared

history.citation: 조셉 스미스의 역사 시간과 계절 (Nauvoo, 일리노이 주) 3, 아니오. 13 (2월 2일 1842):771-73쪽.
history.teaser:
An article from the LDS periodical Times and Seasons connecting the discovery of a catacomb of mummies in Kentucky to the Book of Mormon narrative.

Key Points:

  • Discovery of a catacomb in Lexington, Kentucky in 1775
  • Catacomb contained mummies preserved similarly to ancient Egyptians
  • Discovery linked to ancient town of great extent and magnificence
  • Speculation on the origin and preservation methods of the mummies
  • Article suggests Book of Mormon could solve the mystery
  • Book of Mormon links descendants of Israel to America
  • Embalming knowledge possibly transmitted from Jerusalem
  • Finding of mummies seen as evidence for the Book of Mormon

history.citation: 몰몬교와 맹인. " 뉴욕 헤럴드 (뉴욕) 7, 아니오. 413 (5월 1842일 10).
history.teaser:
An account from Joseph Smith about the early history of his life, including the discovery and translation of the Book of Mormon plates.

Key Points:

  • Joseph Smith recounts obeying a divine messenger’s command
  • Details the discovery of the plates in a stone box
  • Forbidden to take the plates until the appointed time
  • Describes annual visits to the plate’s location for instruction
  • Joseph’s early life involved laboring and moving due to persecution
  • Marriage to Emma Hale amidst family opposition
  • Received assistance from Martin Harris for the translation work
  • Account of Martin Harris’s consultation with scholars about the characters

history.citation: 조셉 스미스의 역사 시간과 계절 (Nauvoo, 일리노이 주) 3, 아니오. 14 (16월 16일 1842):785-86쪽.
history.teaser:
An 1842 New York Herald article discussing Mons. L. de Bonneville’s arrival in New York, who combined mesmerism with Mormon beliefs.

Key Points:

  • Mons. L. de Bonneville arrives in New York, associated with Mormons
  • Formerly a professor at Harvard, now a proponent of Mesmerism and Mormonism
  • Claims to have discovered the true Mormon mode of revelation through Mesmerism
  • Teaches multiple languages and can cure various disorders
  • Abandoned a lucrative position at Harvard for his beliefs
  • Advised to lecture on the connection between Mormonism and Mesmerism

history.citation: 조셉 스미스의 역사 시간과 계절 (Nauvoo, 일리노이 주) 3, 아니오. 15 (1842년 6월 1일):801-4쪽.
history.teaser:
A segment from the “History of Joseph Smith” published in the Times and Seasons detailing the loss of the first 116 pages of the Book of Mormon manuscript.

Key Points:

  • Martin Harris returned to assist Joseph Smith in translation
  • Harris wrote 116 pages of manuscript
  • Harris repeatedly asked to show the writings to others
  • Joseph Smith inquired of the Lord, eventually granted permission with conditions
  • Harris broke his covenant, showing the writings to others and losing them
  • The Urim and Thummim were temporarily taken from Smith
  • A revelation was received chastising Smith and Harris but reaffirming the work’s continuation
  • The revelation also emphasizes the importance and future of the work among the Lamanites

history.citation: Tucker, J. N. T. "몰몬교 - 어떤 호기심이있는 사실" 예언의 Expositor, 3, no. 10 (8월 8일 1842년 6월 8일):79-80쪽.
history.teaser:
A publication detailing a revelation given to Joseph Smith, describing challenges faced during the translation of the Book of Mormon and assurances given by God regarding the continuation and protection of his work.

Key Points:

  • Revelation given after the loss of the initial manuscript
  • Joseph Smith warned against the consequences of trusting the wrong individuals
  • Satan’s influence on people to alter and discredit Joseph’s work highlighted
  • God assures protection against Satan’s attempts to thwart the work
  • Joseph Smith instructed not to retranslate the lost portion
  • Wisdom and commandments given to Joseph Smith for translation work
  • Christ’s intention to gather and protect his followers emphasized
  • Doctrine of the church defined by repentance and coming unto Christ

history.author: 터커, J.N.T.
history.citation: Azteca 국가들 사이에서 발견 된 모자이크 역사의 특성. 시간과 계절 (Nauvoo, 일리노이 주) 3, 아니오. 16 (6월 15일 1842년 6월 15일) : 8 18-20.
history.teaser:
An article by J.N.T. Tucker detailing skepticism and accusations of deceit during the publication of the Book of Mormon.

Key Points:

  • Tucker was a printer during the Book of Mormon’s publication
  • Martin Harris funded the printing
  • Printers tested the translators by claiming to lose a sheet
  • A replacement sheet did not match the original
  • No workers at the printing office converted to Mormonism
  • Tucker claims to witness impostures and false miracles
  • Martin Harris’s wife refused to follow him due to his actions
  • Tucker warns of deception as a sign of the end times

history.citation: 조셉 스미스의 역사 시간과 계절 (Nauvoo, 일리노이 주) 3, 아니오. 16 (6월 15일 1842년 6월 15일):817-8쪽.
history.teaser:
An article discussing the parallels between Mosaic history and Aztec traditions, suggesting common spiritual and historical narratives.

Key Points:

  • Article starts with an Aztec account of the deluge.
  • Draws parallels between Aztec and Biblical stories of Noah.
  • Discusses the confusion of languages, similar to Babel.
  • References to animals and grains saved, paralleling Noah’s Ark.
  • Cites Baron Humboldt’s research on Mexican traditions.
  • Paintings depict the flood and confusion of languages.
  • Links between Aztec traditions and the Book of Mormon.
  • Discussion of the migration to America and the preservation of languages.

history.citation: 리, 존 D., A. Young, Samuel B. Frost. 테네시에서 편지. 시간과 계절 (Nauvoo, 일리노이 주) 3, 아니오. 16 (6월 15일 1842년 6월 15일):820-21쪽.
history.teaser:
An installment from the serialized “History of Joseph Smith” that appeared in the “Times and Seasons” newspaper, discussing revelations received by Joseph Smith.

Key Points:

  • Joseph Smith worked on a farm before continuing translation
  • Revelation received for Joseph Smith, Sr. in February 1829
  • Encouragement to serve God with all heart, might, mind, and strength
  • Qualities that qualify someone for the work of God
  • Revelation given in March 1829 concerning Martin Harris
  • Joseph Smith commanded to show the plates to select individuals
  • Testimony of three witnesses foretold
  • Warnings of consequences for unbelief and disobedience

history.author: 리, 존 D, A. 영, 사무엘 B. 프로스트
history.citation: 몰몬경의 새로운 버전. 시간과 계절 (Nauvoo, 일리노이 주) 3, 아니오. 16 (6월 15일):822쪽.
history.teaser:
A letter detailing the efforts and challenges faced by LDS missionaries in Tennessee, including encounters with false teachings and spiritual manifestations.

Key Points:

  • Report of false teachings in Putnam County, Tennessee
  • False teachers claimed supernatural powers and distorted LDS teachings
  • Described bizarre and violent spiritual manifestations among converts
  • John D. Lee and companions work to correct false teachings
  • Encountered threats of violence and opposition
  • Lee and companions proclaimed against the false spirits and teachings
  • Reported success in restoring sick through faith and priesthood power
  • 28 baptisms in Rutherford, Smith, and Putnam counties

history.citation: 제자. [John E. Page의 질문.] 아침 크로니클 (Pittsburgh, 펜실베니아) (1842년 6월 17일).
history.teaser:
An announcement for the release of a new edition of the Book of Mormon in 1842.

Key Points:

  • New edition of the Book of Mormon has been printed
  • Will be bound and ready for sale in a few days

history.author: 제자들
history.citation: 페이지, John E. [제자에 답장하십시오.] 아침 연대기 (피츠버그, 펜실베니아) (Pitssburgh, 펜실베니아) (1842년 6월 20일).
history.teaser:
A public challenge in a newspaper to John E. Page, an LDS Elder, comparing teachings in LDS scriptures with the Bible.

Key Points:

  • Questioning the relevance of John E. Page’s self-promotion
  • Comparing LDS teachings to traditional Christian teachings
  • Doctrine and Covenants vs. Matthew: Treatment of enemies
  • Book of Mormon vs. Matthew: Response to evil and violence
  • Book of Mormon vs. Romans: Dealing with enemies
  • Seeking clarification on LDS teachings

history.author: 페이지, 존 E.
history.citation: 페이지, 존 E. "몰몬교, 별칭 진리." 아침 Chronicle (피츠버그, 펜실베니아) (1842년 6월 28일).
history.teaser:
John E. Page responds to misinterpretations of Mormon scripture in a Pittsburgh newspaper.

Key Points:

  • John E. Page confirms the accuracy of page references
  • Illustrates misinterpretation using out-of-context Bible quotes
  • Compares scripture misinterpretation to that of LDS texts
  • Highlights the short history of LDS scripture compared to the Bible
  • Notes difficulty in correcting misinterpretations without access to texts
  • Challenges the critic to reveal their real name
  • Defends the integrity of LDS scripture against distortion
  • Identifies himself as an Elder of the LDS Church

history.author: 페이지, 존 E.
history.citation: 제자. [John E. Page에 답장하십시오.] 아침 Chronicle (피츠버그, 펜실베니아) (Pitssburgh, Pennsylvania) (6월 29일 292).
history.teaser:
An article by John E. Page in defense of Mormonism against criticisms and misrepresentations in the press, specifically addressing misconceptions about the Book of Mormon and the Book of Doctrine and Covenants.

Key Points:

  • Defends Mormonism against falsehoods in “The Morning Chronicle”
  • Criticizes the low standards of critics compared to other skeptics
  • Addresses misconceptions about the New Jerusalem in Missouri
  • Clarifies Mormon teachings on acquiring land peacefully
  • Refutes claims that Mormons are commanded to take land by force
  • Highlights the importance of purchasing land to avoid conflict
  • Emphasizes commandments against killing and stealing
  • Condemns the misrepresentation of Mormon doctrines by critics

history.author: 제자들
history.citation: 페이지, 존 E. "몰몬교 별칭, 진실." 아침 크로니클 (피츠버그, 펜실베니아) (6월 30일).
history.teaser:
A letter to the editor questioning the credibility of the Book of Mormon with specific references to its content.

Key Points:

  • Questions about the physical location of the city of Morourhah
  • Description of Jaredite ships likened to dishes and whales
  • Mentions Jaredites’ genealogy extending beyond Adam
  • Claims the Book of Mormon quotes Shakespeare 2000 years early
  • Notes use of a mariner’s compass 600 years before the Christian era
  • Points out contradiction: Jesus’s birthplace as Jerusalem, not Bethlehem
  • Discrepancy in duration of darkness during Crucifixion noted
  • Asserts irreconcilable contradictions between the Bible and the Book of Mormon

history.author: 페이지, 존 E.
history.citation: Pratt, Parley P. Editorial Remarks. 후기 성도의 밀레니엄 별 (리버풀, 영국) 3, 아니오. 3 (7 월 18422):44-47쪽.
history.teaser:
An article by John E. Page defending Mormonism against criticisms, emphasizing divine revelations and the uniqueness of the Latter-day Saint church.

Key Points:

  • Mormons have interactions with angels as biblical figures did
  • Mormonism claims to be the only true church
  • Comparison of the LDS church to ancient Christian church
  • Scriptural basis for the existence of a true church in the last days
  • Misinterpretation and criticism of LDS beliefs addressed
  • Book of Mormon claimed to be written by divine inspiration
  • Assertion that truth will prevail despite persecution
  • John E. Page emphasizes the eternal principle of truth

history.author: Pratt Parsey P. (Parley Parker), 1807-1857
history.citation: 조셉 스미스의 역사 시간과 계절 (Nauvoo, 일리노이 주) 3, 아니오. 17 (1842년 7월 1일):832-33쪽.
history.teaser:
Parley P. Pratt’s editorial in the Millennial Star advocates for the divine origins and purposes of the Latter-Day Saint movement, critiquing contemporary religious practices and emphasizing the need for direct revelation and divine authority.

Key Points:

  • Editorial reflects on God’s purposes and criticizes current religious creeds.
  • Questions the acceptance of Jesus by the present generation.
  • Highlights opposition between God’s ways and human wisdom.
  • Discusses conflicts among religious societies and their impact.
  • Prophesies a “marvellous work and a wonder” through Joseph Smith.
  • Details the providential discovery of the Book of Abraham.
  • Asserts the Book of Abraham’s translation through divine means.
  • Encourages Saints to be receptive to ongoing revelation.

history.citation: 페이지, 존 E. 제자에게. 아침 크로니클 (Pittsburgh, 펜실베니아) (Pitsburgh, Pennsylvania) (1842년 7월 1일).
history.teaser:
An account detailing the arrival of Oliver Cowdery at Joseph Smith’s home and the beginning of their collaboration on translating the Book of Mormon, including a revelation encouraging their work.

Key Points:

  • Oliver Cowdery came to inquire about the plates in April 1829
  • Translation of the Book of Mormon began on April 17, 1829
  • A revelation was received encouraging the translation work
  • God’s word described as quick, powerful, and capable of enlightenment
  • Commanded to seek not riches but wisdom and to bring forth Zion
  • Oliver Cowdery is encouraged to use his gift for God’s work
  • The importance of being faithful and diligent in keeping commandments
  • Promise of Jesus Christ’s presence in the midst of their work

history.author: 페이지, 존 E.
history.citation: 세르 린, 메피 보츠. 시간과 계절 (Nauvoo, 일리노이 주) 3, 아니오. 17 (7월 1일 18422):838-39쪽.
history.teaser:
An article by John E. Page in the Morning Chronicle addressing criticisms of the Book of Mormon and affirming its authenticity through scriptural and archaeological references.

Key Points:

  • Refers to Isaiah to defend the Book of Mormon
  • Discusses the Book of Mormon’s prediction of ancient American cities
  • Mentions Mr. Anthon’s encounter with characters from the plates
  • Addresses the location of the city of Moronihah
  • Claims the Book of Mormon will be ranked with the Bible
  • Counters accusations of inaccuracies in the Book of Mormon
  • Defends the Book of Mormon’s account of Christ’s birth
  • Challenges critics and defends the truth of the Book of Mormon

history.author: 세린, 메피보세
history.citation: 제자. [John E. Page에 답장하십시오.] 아침 크로니클 (피츠버그, 펜실베니아) (Pitssburgh, Pennsylvania) (1842년 7월 2일).
history.teaser:
A letter published in the “Times and Seasons” describing the missionary efforts and public debate in Michigan that resulted in support for the Book of Mormon.

Key Points:

  • Mephibosheth Serrine reports on spreading the truth in Michigan
  • Visited different churches; found them generally prosperous
  • Held two-day meetings, leading to baptisms and interest
  • Faced opposition from various religious leaders
  • Engaged in a public debate on the Book of Mormon’s divinity
  • Debate resulted in a decision favoring the Book of Mormon
  • Some attendees lost faith in Methodism after the debate
  • Serrine sees this as part of the Book of Mormon’s prophecy fulfillment

history.author: 제자들
history.citation: 페이지, 요한 E. "몰몬경은 옹호되었습니다." 아침 Chronicle (피츠버그, 펜실베니아) (7월 2일).
history.teaser:
A critical letter in the Morning Chronicle addressing discrepancies between the Book of Mormon and the Bible.

Key Points:

  • Author challenges Elder Page without personal animosity
  • Points out anachronisms and inconsistencies in the Book of Mormon
  • Highlights differences between the 1st and 3rd editions of the Book of Mormon
  • Claims the Book of Mormon contradicts the Bible on Jesus’s birthplace and the duration of darkness at his crucifixion
  • Asserts that both records cannot be true; one must be false
  • Concludes the Bible is true, thus the Book of Mormon must be false
  • Uses the metaphor “Dagon has fallen before the ark of the Lord” to illustrate his point

history.author: 페이지, 존 E.
history.citation: 제자. [John E. Page에 답장하십시오.] 아침 Chronicle (피츠버그, 펜실베니아) (Patsburgh, 펜실베니아) (1842년 7월 7일).
history.teaser:
An article by John E. Page defending Mormonism against claims made in “Mormonism Unveiled,” specifically addressing the theory that Sidney Rigdon created the Book of Mormon from a manuscript by Solomon Spaulding.

Key Points:

  • Page refutes the claim that Rigdon authored the Book of Mormon.
  • Benjamin Winchester’s testimony is used to discredit “Mormonism Unveiled.”
  • “Mormonism Unveiled” suggests Rigdon used a Spaulding manuscript.
  • Rigdon’s timeline disputes his ability to have used the manuscript.
  • Mrs. Davidson (Spaulding’s widow) had the manuscript, not Rigdon.
  • Page argues against the credibility of “Mormonism Unveiled.”
  • The article illustrates the lengths to which enemies of Mormonism will go.
  • Compares persecution of Mormons to that of early Christians.

history.author: 제자들
history.document: 존 E. 페이지 장로에게 묻고 싶은 몇 가지 질문이 있습니다.
history.citation: 페이지, 존 E. "몰몬교, 별칭 진리." 아침 크로니클 (피츠버그, 펜실베니아) (Pennsylvania) (1842년 7월 8일).
history.teaser:
A critical editorial questioning the teachings and intentions of Mormonism, as addressed to Elder John E. Page.

Key Points:

  • Questions if Mormonism intends to supersede Christianity
  • Compares Joseph Smith to Moses and Jesus as a religious author
  • Asks if the Book of Mormon sets aside the Old and New Testaments
  • Questions why Mormons don’t baptize into Joseph Smith
  • Inquires about divine confirmation of Joseph Smith’s authority
  • Contrasts peaceful prophetic visions with Joseph Smith’s military actions
  • Claims Mormons consider America their promised land
  • Questions if Mormons will attempt to expel non-believers from America
  • Accuses Mormonism of promoting conversion through force
  • Alleges Joseph Smith required a bodyguard for suspicion of assassination involvement
  • Claims assassination is commanded for dissenters within Mormonism
  • Asserts Mormonism aims to establish a Western Empire

history.author: 페이지, 존 E.
history.citation: 제자. [John E. Page에 답장하십시오.] 아침 크로니클 (피츠버그, 펜실베니아) (Pitssburgh, 펜실베니아) (1842년 7월 9일).

  • Rigdon agrees to investigate the Book of Mormon’s claims
  • Many in Kirtland, including Rigdon, eventually accept the Book of Mormon
  • Rigdon convinced of the Book of Mormon’s truth through personal revelation

history.citation: 체계적 솔직 및 일관성 T. C. 존슨에게 알렉산더 캠벨. 밀레니엄 Harbinger 7, NO. 12 (12 월 1843):553-57쪽.
history.teaser:
An article from a Latter-day Saint publication discussing the significance of Stephens’ explorations in Central America to the Book of Mormon.

Key Points:

  • Stephens’ work details ancient, sophisticated civilizations in America
  • Work has passed through twelve editions, indicating widespread interest
  • Stephens made further explorations with the Daguerreotype
  • His findings are seen as supporting the Book of Mormon
  • Stephens visited ancient cities, aligning with Book of Mormon accounts
  • Describes ruins as evidence of a once mighty people
  • Book of Mormon published years before these discoveries
  • Explorations considered strong circumstantial evidence for the Book of Mormon

history.author: 존슨, T.C.
history.citation: 브라운, 헨리. 일리노이의 역사는 첫 번째 발견과 정착지에서 현재 시간, 394. 뉴욕 : J. Winchester, New World Press, 1844.
history.teaser:
A letter by T. C. Johnson to Alexander Campbell discussing the misconceptions and misrepresentations of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (LDS Church) and its doctrines as compared to those of Alexander Campbell and his followers.

Key Points:

  • Johnson critiques a book that conflates Mormonism with Campbellism.
  • The book claims early Mormons were influenced by Alexander Campbell.
  • Johnson argues the book falsely associates Campbell’s teachings with Mormonism.
  • Johnson points out the absurdity of linking Mormon baptism practices to Campbellism.
  • Methodism, by the author’s logic, could also be linked to Mormonism.
  • Johnson defends the original teachings of Campbell against accusations of similarity to Mormon doctrine.
  • He criticizes the Methodist Episcopal Church for endorsing the book’s misrepresentations.
  • Johnson calls for fairness, truth, and preparation for divine judgment.

history.author: 브라운, 헨리, 1789-1849
history.citation: 사냥, 제임스 H. <i>몰몬교 : 몰몬경의 검사와 함께 종파의 원산지, 상승 및 진행 상승 및 진행; 또한, 미주리의 그들의 문제, 그리고 St. Louis : Usk & Davies, 1844.
history.teaser:
An 1844 critique of the Book of Mormon and the Latter Day Saints, comparing their beliefs and practices unfavorably with traditional Christianity.

Key Points:

  • Book of Mormon held in same veneration as New Testament
  • Author skeptical of the Book of Mormon’s authenticity
  • Mormons’ story seen as implausible by the author
  • Comparison with other contemporary “impostures”
  • Age described as “an age of humbugs”
  • Gold plates no longer exist, arousing suspicion
  • Law of Moses on stone vs. Mormon law on gold plates
  • Contrast between Christ’s actions and Mormon prophet’s goals

history.author: 헌트, 제임스 H
history.citation: Baird, Robert. <i>미국의 종교 : 또는 국가의 관계, 국가의 관계, 미국의 복음주의 교회의 현재 상태, 647- 49. 글래스고 : Blackieands Son, 1844.
history.teaser:
A critical examination of the origins, beliefs, and historical conflicts of Mormonism, focusing on its development and the controversies surrounding the Book of Mormon.

Key Points:

  • Objective to provide a factual account of conflicts in Missouri
  • Focuses on denouncing wrongdoings by both Mormons and Missourians
  • Includes an examination of the Book of Mormon
  • Covers the rise and progress of the Mormon sect
  • Discusses the expulsion of Mormons from Missouri
  • Appendix details disturbances in Illinois leading to the Smiths’ deaths
  • Intends to correct falsehoods spread by Mormons
  • Published shortly after the death of Joseph and Hyrum Smith

history.author: 베어드, 로버트
history.citation: 루이스, R. B. 가볍고 진실; 성경과 고대, 현대적인 역사에서 징수 된 색깔과 인도 인도의 보편적 인 역사를 포함하는 역사, 34. 보스턴 : 1844 년 착색 한위원회.
history.teaser:
A critical examination of the origins and development of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (Mormons) by Robert Baird, highlighting perceived fraudulence and delusion.

Key Points:

  • Mormonism seen as an example of cunning leadership and deluded followers
  • Joseph Smith claimed to receive golden plates from an angel in 1827
  • Book of Mormon published as a result of these revelations
  • Book of Mormon is not considered a substitute but a supplement to the Bible
  • Joseph Smith also attempted a new translation of the Bible
  • Origins of Mormonism traced to the publication of the Book of Mormon in 1830
  • Mormons moved to several locations, facing opposition, before settling in Nauvoo, Illinois
  • Leaders criticized for ambition and character, leading to predictions of the sect’s demise

history.author: 루이스, R.B. (로버트 벤자민)
history.citation: 에반스, 존. L. L. D. 모든 기독교 분파와 교단의 역사; 그들의 기원, 특이한 교리 및 현재 상태. 무신론자, 신청사, 유대인, 미혼학생, 이교도, & c의 입문 계좌로 , 15 번째 런던 에디션에서. 개수는 확대되었습니다. 2nd., 232-33. 뉴욕 : James Mowatt & Co., 1844.
history.teaser:
A historical account linking the genealogy of Joseph from the Bible to the peoples described in the Book of Mormon, emphasizing connections to Egyptian and Ethiopian heritage.

Key Points:

  • Joseph’s sons Manasseh and Ephraim lead to Manassehites and Ephraimites
  • Descendants include various tribes such as Machirites and Gileadites
  • Zelophehad’s daughters listed, showing female lineage importance
  • Claims Manasseh’s descendants were Egyptians or Ethiopians
  • Book of Mormon peoples are descendants of Joseph and Ishmael
  • Lehi’s sons were Laman, Lemuel, Sam, and Nephi
  • Lehi’s sons married daughters of Ishmael, described as “dark red people”
  • Emphasizes a genealogical link between biblical figures and Book of Mormon peoples

history.author: 에반스, 존, 1767-1827
history.citation: Adams, George J. 몰몬경, 1-24의 진정성 및 성서의 성격의 강의. 보스턴 : J. E. Farwell, 1844.
history.teaser:
An early and critical overview of the origins, beliefs, and spread of the Latter-Day Saint movement, focusing on the Book of Mormon.

Key Points:

  • Book of Mormon published in 1830
  • Doctrines zealously propagated throughout the United States and Canada
  • Thousands of converts in England, missionaries sent to Palestine
  • Book of Mormon claims history of a pre-Columbian American people
  • Records engraved on plates, deposited in Hill Cumorah, New York
  • Joseph Smith Jr. found the plates in 1825, translated them
  • Translation claimed to be by divine inspiration
  • Smith’s account of obtaining the plates included in a 1842 letter

history.author: 아담스, 조지 J. (조지 존스), 1811-1880
history.document: 몰몬교의 진위여부와 성서적 특성에 관한 강의
history.citation: Merrill, Joseph W. 인민 캐비닛 : 자연사의 주제에 대한 Compendium; 자연 철학; 천문학; 헌법, 조직 및 인체의 기능; 마음과 그 능력; 미국의 역사 : 정부와 법, 특히 미국의; 또한 다양한 종교 교단의 신념; 세계 모든 연령층에서 고유 한 캐릭터의 전기 스케치, 279-80. 보스턴 : Joseph W. Merrill, 1844.
history.teaser:
A lecture by George J. Adams advocating for the authenticity and scriptural alignment of the Book of Mormon, delivered in Charlestown, Massachusetts, in 1844.

Key Points:

  • Addressed misconceptions about the Latter Day Saints’ beliefs.
  • Argued that the Book of Mormon is foretold by biblical prophecy.
  • Presented the Book of Mormon as a continuation of biblical revelation.
  • Emphasized unity between the Book of Mormon and the Bible.
  • Highlighted scriptural references indicating the coming of an additional book.
  • Discussed the prophecy of a sealed book understood by the unlearned.
  • Connected the coming forth of the Book of Mormon to the gathering of Israel.
  • Encouraged scrutiny of scriptures to find truth and understanding.

history.author: 메릴, 조셉 W.
history.citation: Raumer, Fredrich Von. 미국과 미국인, 334-36. 1844.
history.teaser:
A comprehensive overview of the beliefs of the Latter Day Saints as presented in The People’s Cabinet, highlighting the foundational role of the Book of Mormon in Mormonism.

Key Points:

  • The Book of Mormon was first published in 1830
  • It records the history of people in America before Columbus
  • Joseph Smith, Jr. found and translated the plates by God’s direction
  • Belief in God, Jesus Christ, and the Holy Ghost
  • Salvation through Christ and obedience to gospel ordinances
  • Ordinances include faith, repentance, baptism, and laying on of hands
  • Belief in the organization of the primitive church
  • Belief in the Bible and Book of Mormon as God’s word

history.author: 라우머, 프레드리히 폰 (1781-1873)
history.citation: 몰몬교의 책 (팔미라, N. y.) (1844).
history.teaser:
A historical account by Fredrich von Raumer regarding Joseph Smith, the founding of Mormonism, and early conflicts involving Mormons.

Key Points:

  • Joseph Smith characterized as lively and cunning
  • Smith announced a new revelation in 1827
  • Smith refused to produce the original tablets
  • Smith gained numerous followers despite skepticism
  • Mormons faced opposition and settled in Mississippi
  • Governor Dunklin advocated for religious freedom
  • Mormons’ views conflicted with democratic institutions
  • Smith’s death did not change the course of opposition

history.citation: 그레그, 요시야. 대초원의 상거래 : 또는 Santa Fé Trader의 저널, 8 멋진 서방의 대초원을 가로 질러 원정대, 북부 멕시코에서 거의 9 년의 거주지. 1, 312-20. 뉴욕 : Langley & Astor, 1844.
history.teaser:
A broadside promoting the Book of Mormon in 1844, linking it to biblical prophecies and the narrative of a sacred text lost and found.

Key Points:

  • Title refers to the Stick of Joseph, from Ephraim
  • Contains a copy of characters from the Book of Mormon plates
  • Characters were shown to Professor Anthon by Martin Harris in 1827
  • Links the story to Isaiah 28. 11, 12 about a sealed book
  • Quotes Psalm 85:11 about truth springing from the earth
  • References Hosea 8:12 about God’s laws given to Ephraim
  • Ezekiel 37:19 prophecy about joining the sticks of Joseph and Judah
  • Mentions an aged Indian’s lament about a lost sacred book

history.author: 그레그, 조시아, 1806-1850
history.citation: Appleby, W. I. Nepuchadnezzar의 꿈의 논문 : 다니엘의 왕국이 사도들의 시대에 설치되지 않았습니다. 그리고 왕국의 순서가 설명 된 다음 설명했습니다. 또한 : 현재의 주목할만한 정통 사회의 상승과 신앙은 "후기 성도 교회 교회 교회의 신앙과 다른 사회의 신앙을 비교하여 1-24 ...에 필라델피아 : 브라운, Bicking & Guilbert, 1844.
history.teaser:
An account by Josiah Gregg detailing the conflicts between early Mormons and their Missouri neighbors, leading to the Mormons’ expulsion.

Key Points:

  • Mormons originally selected Independence, Missouri, for their New Jerusalem.
  • Conflicts arose due to alleged Mormon thefts and immorality.
  • Increasing Mormon population threatened local control, leading to violence.
  • A mob destroyed a Mormon printing establishment and punished leaders.
  • Joseph Smith, the Mormon leader, was not present during conflicts.
  • Mormons eventually surrendered and were forced to leave the area.
  • After moving to Clay County, Mormons faced further conflicts and moved again.
  • Mormons refused to sell Missouri property, aiming to reconquer it.

history.author: 애플비, W.I. (윌리엄 아이빈스), 1811-1870
history.citation: C., A. (Alexander Campbell). "몰몬경을 만지는 실수." 밀레엔엔제 Harbinger 1, NO. 1 (1844년 1월):38-42쪽.
history.teaser:
A summary of an 1844 document by W. I. Appleby providing a detailed account of the early history, beliefs, and experiences of Joseph Smith, founder of the Latter Day Saint movement, including his first visions, the reception of the Book of Mormon, and the establishment of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-Day Saints.

Key Points:

  • Joseph Smith’s early visions and visitations by angels
  • Reception and translation of the Book of Mormon
  • Establishment of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-Day Saints in 1830
  • Belief in living prophets and continuous revelation
  • Emphasis on obedience to God’s commandments and ordinances
  • Persecutions faced by early Latter-Day Saints
  • Rapid growth and missionary work of the Church globally
  • Assertion of the Church’s divine origin and destiny to prevail

history.author: 캠벨, 알렉산더, 1788-1866
history.citation: 고대 유적 시간과 계절 (Nauvoo, 일리노이 주) 5, 아니오. 1 (1844년 1월 1일):390-91쪽.
history.teaser:
A critique by Alexander Campbell on misconceptions regarding the Book of Mormon’s origins and teachings, specifically addressing the concept of baptism for the remission of sins.

Key Points:

  • Mormonism accused of stealing the true gospel
  • Rigdon said to have learned gospel elements before meeting Smith
  • Baptism for remission of sins is indeed found in the Book of Mormon
  • Misconceptions about the origin and teachings of the Book of Mormon addressed
  • Campbell refutes claims baptism for remission wasn’t initially part of Mormon doctrine
  • Discussion on the public and internal Christian debate regarding baptism
  • Campbell advocates for correct understanding and practice of baptism
  • Emphasizes importance of addressing misconceptions for unity and clarity within Christian beliefs

An article discussing the discovery of ancient ruins in America, supporting the authenticity of the Book of Mormon’s account of advanced ancient civilizations on the continent.

Key Points:

  • Fresh testimony supports the Book of Mormon’s authenticity
  • Discovery of ancient cities challenges previous beliefs
  • Stephens’ travels add evidence of advanced ancient civilizations
  • Ruins found in Northern Texas and between Santa Fe and the Pacific
  • Immense ruins of an ancient temple described
  • Architecture not attributed to Spaniards or Europeans
  • Ruins believed to resemble Palenque or Otulum
  • Speculation about connections to the Aztic or Toltec races

history.citation: 성경과 몰몬경 .- 예언. 보스턴 조사관 (1844년 1월 17일).
history.teaser:
An article from the “Times and Seasons” discussing the concept of the gathering of the saints, its biblical precedents, and its theological significance.

Key Points:

  • Gathering of saints seen as strange by the religious world.
  • Gathering is a principle Jehovah has acted upon throughout history.
  • All nations shall flock to Zion, established in righteousness.
  • God’s plans for humanity are comprehensive and wise.
  • Everything created by God was for a purpose and His glory.
  • Different glories for different beings in the afterlife.
  • The earth will be purified and become celestial.
  • Prophets and apostles sought a celestial inheritance through faith.

An article from the Boston Investigator proposing the idea that the Bible and the Book of Mormon originated in similar manners and predicting the eventual incorporation of the Book of Mormon into the Bible and the LDS Church becoming a major religious force.

Key Points:

  • Proposes similarity in origin between the Bible and the Book of Mormon
  • Predicts Mormonism will become the predominant religious sect
  • Book of Mormon will be incorporated into the Bible
  • Old and New Testaments and the Book of Mormon were “found”
  • Councils confirmed the canonical status of Biblical books
  • Mormonism’s growth attributed to its adaptation to the times
  • Persecution predicted to increase Mormonism’s followers
  • Asserts the inevitability of Mormonism’s predominance based on current trends

history.citation: [G. W. M. br. Whittemore 1 월 18444년 1월] "몰몬교,"트럼펫과 유니버얼리스트 잡지 (보스턴) 16, 아니오. 37 (3월 2일 3월 2일):1쪽. 몰몬교.
history.teaser:
An article discussing the biblical and Book of Mormon teachings on the scattering and gathering of Israel, emphasizing God’s continuous care and plan for all branches of the house of Israel.

Key Points:

  • Jared, his brother, and their descendants blessed but eventually swept away
  • Abraham chosen to preserve God’s laws and ordinances through his seed
  • Provisions made for preserving a remnant of Israel in various lands
  • Lehi and Ishmael’s families directed to the Americas
  • Ten Tribes taken to a distant land to be gathered in the latter days
  • Parable of the olive tree in the Book of Mormon explained
  • Some branches of Israel hidden, explaining why not all were known historically
  • Jesus Christ’s teachings in the Book of Mormon about other sheep not of the Jerusalem fold

history.author: 미스터, G.W.
history.citation: 몰몬교 보스턴 조사관 (5월 22일).
history.teaser:
An article challenging the association between Mormonism and the doctrine of Universal Salvation, using the Book of Mormon.

Key Points:

  • Elder E. J. Adams delivers lectures on Mormonism in Boston
  • Article questions whether Mormonism teaches Universal Salvation
  • Book of Mormon teaches the Trinity and a personal Devil
  • Adam’s immortality and a state of probation discussed
  • Book of Mormon supports the concept of an infinite atonement
  • Endless misery for the wicked endorsed, against Universal Salvation
  • Preaching Universal Salvation as Mormon belief seen as dishonest
  • Mormons urged to preach their own faith accurately

history.citation: 리드 (Reed, John S.) "John S. Reed의 발언, Esq., Thestate 협약 이전에 배달 된 것처럼." 시간과 계절 5, no. 11 (1 일 1 일 1 일 1 일 1):549-52쪽.
history.teaser:
An 1844 newspaper article from the Boston Investigator discussing the growth and normalization of the Mormon community in Nauvoo, including their engagement in theatrical productions.

Key Points:

  • New York Aurora reports on a theatre in Nauvoo
  • The play Pizarro performed to a large audience
  • Prediction that Mormons will become a significant sect
  • Comparison of Mormon leaders to founders of other sects
  • Joseph Smith’s claims of divine inspiration not unique
  • Reference to other religious founders claiming divine inspiration
  • Future acceptance of Mormons predicted

history.document: John S의 발언 중 일부. 리드
history.citation: [Pratt, Parley P.] Joe Smith와 악마 : 대화. " 뉴욕 헤럴드 (뉴욕) 10, 아니오. 236 (8월 25일 2544). [해독되지 않음]
history.teaser:
John S. Reed’s account of early persecutions faced by Joseph Smith, emphasizing his innocence and integrity.

Key Points:

  • John S. Reed defends Joseph Smith’s character and early history
  • Joseph Smith faced persecution from professed Christians
  • Smith’s character described as irreproachable and intelligent
  • Smith had revelations about finding golden plates
  • Smith was arrested and tried multiple times but found not guilty
  • Reed viewed Smith as predestined by God for a great work
  • Smith’s religious opinions were the main cause of persecution
  • Reed believed God assisted in Smith’s protection and success

history.author: [Pratt, Parsey P.]
history.citation: 몰몬 종파의 상승과 파멸. " 회중 잡지 (1844년 9월):641-649쪽.
history.teaser:
A satirical piece by Parley P. Pratt presenting a fictional dialogue between Joseph Smith and the Devil, published in The New York Herald.

Key Points:

  • Devil seeking to recruit against Joseph Smith and the Mormons
  • Devil claims Joseph Smith caused him more trouble than others
  • Joseph Smith denies causing trouble, adheres to Mormon creed
  • Devil admits respect for all forms of Christianity except direct revelation
  • Joseph Smith challenges the Devil’s opposition to new revelation
  • Devil acknowledges inability to counter Smith’s arguments
  • Devil admits to spreading falsehoods but blames clergy and editors
  • Ending with a humorous reconciliation and a toast between Smith and the Devil

history.citation: D., E. "Mormon 신앙과 사람들의 상승과 진보" 남부 문학 메신저 10 (1844년 9월):526-38쪽.
history.teaser:
An article from The Congregational Magazine providing a critical overview of the rise of Mormonism and the violent death of its founder, Joseph Smith.

Key Points:

  • Joseph Smith’s tragic death announced
  • Smith’s history and claimed revelations discussed
  • Accusations of fraud and the Spaulding manuscript theory mentioned
  • Smith’s narrative of angelic visitations and finding golden plates
  • Critique of the Book of Mormon’s content and claims
  • Persecution and migration of Mormons to Missouri and Illinois
  • Narrative of Smith’s downfall, including charges and mob violence
  • Smith and his brother Hyrum’s deaths in jail by an armed mob

history.author: D., E.
history.citation: 고대 유적 시간과 계절 (Nauvoo, 일리노이 주) 5, 아니오. 23 (1844년 12월 15일):744-48쪽.
history.teaser:
An article from the “Southern Literary Messenger” detailing the history, beliefs, and practices of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (Mormons) and their founder, Joseph Smith.

Key Points:

  • Article explores the rise and doctrines of the Mormon church.
  • Joseph Smith’s revelations and translations form the basis of Mormonism.
  • The Book of Mormon is considered a historical and religious record.
  • Mormons believe in modern-day revelation and prophecy.
  • Nauvoo, Illinois, serves as a central gathering place for Mormons.
  • The article critiques the logic and consistency of Mormon beliefs.
  • Mormon missionaries extend their reach globally, even to Jerusalem and India.
  • The rapid growth of Mormonism reflects a deep human yearning for spiritual guidance.

history.citation: 고대 유적 <i> 시간과 계절 </ i> (Nauvoo, 일리노이 주) 5, 아니오. 23 (1844 년 12 월 15 일) : 744-48.
history.teaser:
An article from the Times and Seasons discussing the significance of ancient ruins in relation to scriptural prophecy and the divine history of the earth as understood by the Latter-Day Saints.

Key Points:

  • Discussion on civilizations before and after Noah’s flood
  • Prophecy fulfillment seen in discovery of ancient ruins
  • Contemporary speculations on ruins compared to scriptural accounts
  • Ruins as evidence of God’s actions on earth
  • Scriptural references to the scattering of people at Babel
  • Comparisons between ancient and modern acts of greatness and folly
  • Book of Mormon as a source for understanding ancient American civilizations
  • Calls for recognition of revelation in understanding ruins and divine history
